PostgreSQL

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

DefaultContextDelegatedResponse augmentation in @strapi/core is never attached to Context, so error-response helpers type as any

`@strapi/core/dist/index.d.ts` declares:

```
declare module 'koa' {
  interface DefaultContextDelegatedResponse
    extends ContextDelegatedResponseErrorMethods, ContextDelegatedResponseSuccessMethods {}
}
```

but nothing in `@types/koa` (2.15.0) references `DefaultContextDelegatedResponse` — it's not extended by Context, BaseContext, or ExtendableContext. So this interface is orphaned and never merges into Koa.Context.

At runtime `ctx.badRequest`, `ctx.internalServerError`, etc. work fine (Strapi patches them in), but by types they don't exist as declared members. TypeScript doesn't error on `ctx.internalServerError(...)` though — it silently resolves to any, because `@types/koa's` `DefaultContext` has a catch-all `[key: PropertyKey]: any`. This means calls like `ctx.internalServerError(someCaughtError)` (where `someCaughtError: unknown`) type-check even though the real signature is (`response?: string | object, details?: object) => void` — no compile-time safety at all on these helpers.


### Steps to Reproduce

`npm i @strapi/core@5.51.0 @types/koa@2.15.0`, then in a controller:

```
import type { Context } from 'koa'
declare const ctx: Context
ctx.internalServerError // typed as `any`, should be `(response?: string | object, details?: object) => void`
```


### Expected Behavior

extend `BaseContext` (or `ExtendableContext`) directly, e.g.:


```
declare module 'koa' {
  interface BaseContext
    extends ContextDelegatedResponseErrorMethods, ContextDelegatedResponseSuccessMethods {}
}
```

### Node Version

22.23.2

### Package Manager

yarn

### Package Manager Version

4.12.0

### Strapi Version

`develop` with #27557

### Operating System

MacOS

### Database

SQLite

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/27557

### Bug Description

Cloning a document with a media override expressed as a relation operation payload, such as `{ set: [...] }`, can silently keep the source document's media instead of applying the override.

This is related to, but not caused by, #27557. That PR makes media document IDs usable in the Document Service create/update transform. The clone behavior predates it; before #27557, a document-ID media payload failed validation earlier instead of reaching the incorrect clone merge.

The clone helper protects relation operation overrides from being mixed with populated source data, but its traversal only recognizes relation attributes. Media attributes are not collected and restored after the source and submitted data are merged.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a collection type with a single-media field such as `cover`.
2. Upload two files, A and B.
3. Create a source document whose `cover` is A.
4. Clone the source document through the Document Service or clone endpoint and override `cover` with `{ set: [{ documentId: '<file-B-document-id>' }] }`.
5. Populate `cover` on the cloned document.
6. Observe that the clone still references A instead of B, without an error.

The same area should be checked for `connect` and `disconnect` media payloads and for media nested in components or dynamic zones.

### Expected Behavior

A media operation override supplied during clone should be preserved and applied exactly like a relation operation override. In the example above, the cloned document should reference B. The original document must remain unchanged.

### Logs

```shell
No error is emitted; the clone succeeds with the wrong media value.
```

### Code Snippets

```ts
await strapi.documents('api::article.article').clone({
  documentId: sourceDocumentId,
  data: {
    cover: { set: [{ documentId: fileBDocumentId }] },
  },
});
```

Relevant code: `packages/core/core/src/services/document-service/utils/clone-relations.ts`. `collectRelationOperationOverrides` uses relation traversal, so media operation payloads are not restored after merging the original and submitted data.

### Additional information

Raised during review of #27557. PR #27116 separately handles single-media last-wins enforcement and does not address clone override preservation.

### Confirmation Checklist

- [x] I have checked the existing issues for duplicates.
- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct.

### Node Version

v22.20.0

### Package Manager

yarn

### Package Manager Version

4.12.0

### Strapi Version

`develop` at #27505 (MCP TypeScript SDK v2). Content-manager does not register prompts today; the defect is in prompt registration and `prompts/list`.

### Operating System

MacOS

### Database

SQLite

### Javascript or Typescript

TypeScript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

Registering one MCP prompt whose `argsSchema` cannot be converted to JSON Schema succeeds with no error. The prompt stays `enabled` in the registry. The next `prompts/list` then fails with JSON-RPC `-32603` and **returns no prompts at all**. Healthy sibling prompts disappear from discovery even though `prompts/get` on those names still works.

Verified unconvertible types include `z.date()`, `z.coerce.date()`, `z.custom()`, `z.instanceof()`, and `z.bigint()`. The listed error for `z.date()` is `Date cannot be represented in JSON Schema`.

This is not a handler bug. `registerPrompt` only asks the SDK to inspect the Zod shape for completable fields. Conversion runs later, unguarded, inside the SDK v2 `prompts/list` handler. `createSafeCapabilityRegistration` never sees the throw, so it cannot disable the bad prompt.

`resources/list` is unaffected. `tools/list` has the same hole when a tool carries an unconvertible field, but that path already failed on SDK 1.30 (`5.52.2`). The prompt-side failure is new with SDK v2: listing still ships only `{ name, description, required }` per argument, yet v2 converts the full schema to derive that metadata.

Found during QA of #27505. Out of scope for that PR. Documented there as breaking change 2.

Upstream conversion failure: [modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk#2464](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/issues/2464).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable MCP (`server.mcp.enabled: true`).
2. Register two prompts. Give one a JSON-representable `argsSchema` (`z.string()`, `z.number()`, …). Give the other an unconvertible field, for example `z.date()`.
3. Confirm `registerPrompt` returns success and both registry entries are `enabled`.
4. Call `prompts/list` through a real MCP client.

### Expected Behavior

- Registration of an unconvertible `argsSchema` fails or disables that prompt, with a server log naming it.
- `prompts/list` still returns every healthy prompt.
- A conversion error on one prompt does not become `-32603` for the whole list.

### Logs

```
-32603 "Date cannot be represented in JSON Schema"
```

`prompts/list` returns no prompts. Direct `prompts/get` on a healthy sibling still succeeds.

### Code Snippets

```ts
// Registration succeeds. prompts/list then fails for every prompt.
argsSchema: z.object({
  due: z.date().describe('Due date'),
});

// Lists correctly.
argsSchema: z.object({
  due: z.string().datetime().describe('Due date as ISO-8601'),
});
```

`createSafeCapabilityRegistration` (`packages/core/core/src/services/mcp/utils/createSafeCapabilityRegistration.ts`) catches SDK registration errors only. SDK v2 does not convert the schema at `registerPrompt` time, so the catch never fires.

### Media

_No response_

### Additional information

Reproduced in-process against `createMcpServerWithRegistries` with a real MCP client over an in-memory transport, and cross-checked against `develop` on SDK 1.30.

QA source: [giu1io's review on #27505](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/27505#pullrequestreview-5137372368).

Related docs-only issue: #27558. This ticket is the product defect, not the guide wording.

- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

items.body:
### Node Version

24.18.0 (`node:24-alpine` image)

### Package Manager

npm

### Package Manager Version

11.16.0

### Strapi Version

5.48.1 (version running when the incident occurred). The affected code path is unchanged in the current release 5.52.3 and on `develop` as of 2026-09-07, see the source references below.

### Operating System

Docker/Podman/LXC

### Database

MySQL

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

The internal migration runner has **no concurrency protection**. When two instances of the same app boot at the same time against the same database (e.g. a Kubernetes deployment with `replicas: 2` rolling out the v5 upgrade image), both instances see all internal migrations as pending and run them concurrently.

`core::5.0.0-discard-drafts` is not idempotent, so the second run inserts an additional draft row for every published entry.

This hit us in production during the v4→v5 upgrade. Two pods booted the new image within seconds of each other and both ran the internal migrations. `strapi_migrations_internal` records the double run literally (three migration names logged twice, see Logs). The result was **731 duplicate-row groups** across single types, collection types and components (~2,800 documents). The damage is not cosmetic: publishing clones every draft row of a document, so the stale duplicate can win, documents get stuck in the "Modified" state and republish outdated content. Recovery required a multi-week, hand-verified in-place deduplication of the production database. Restoring a backup and re-running the migration was not an option because that mints new random `documentId`s and breaks every stored reference.

**Where the guard is missing (verified in source on `develop`):**

1. **The runner is check-then-act.** [`packages/core/database/src/migrations/runner.ts`](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/packages/core/database/src/migrations/runner.ts): `up()` reads the tracking table, filters pending migrations, executes each one, and calls `storage.logMigration()` only **after** the migration body succeeded. For a data migration that runs for minutes, that is a very wide race window. (In 5.48.1 this was Umzug with the same custom storage; the new in-house runner on `develop` keeps the same check-then-act shape.)
2. **No lock anywhere.** [`packages/core/database/src/migrations/storage.ts`](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/packages/core/database/src/migrations/storage.ts) creates the tracking table with `id`, `name`, `time` only: no lock table, no `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, no advisory lock, and **no unique constraint on `name`**, so the second runner does not even fail on the log insert.
3. **The per-migration transaction does not help.** [`packages/core/database/src/migrations/internal.ts`](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/packages/core/database/src/migrations/internal.ts) wraps each migration in a transaction. That makes one run atomic, but two concurrent transactions from two instances both see an empty tracking table and both commit.
4. **The protection exists one layer down and is not used.** Strapi uses Knex as query builder but not Knex's migration API, which ships exactly this guard (`knex_migrations_lock`: ["A lock system is there to prevent multiple processes from running the same migration batch in the same time"](https://knexjs.org/guide/migrations.html)).
5. **`discard-drafts` is not idempotent.** [`packages/core/core/src/migrations/database/5.0.0-discard-drafts.ts`](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/packages/core/core/src/migrations/database/5.0.0-discard-drafts.ts): the draft clone is an `INSERT INTO … SELECT … WHERE published_at IS NOT NULL` with no `NOT EXISTS` guard. The relation join inserts use duplicate handling (`onConflict().ignore()` / insert-or-ignore), the content-table insert does not, so a second run silently duplicates data instead of failing.

The same lack of locking applies to the other write phases of `strapi.load()` (schema sync DDL and the `afterSync` hooks), but the internal migration runner is where the data damage happened, so this report focuses on it.

**Documentation contradiction:** the [database migrations docs](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/database-migrations) state that *"applied migrations are tracked so they never run twice."* With more than one instance booting concurrently this is not true. Neither the [v4→v5 upgrade guide](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/migration/v4-to-v5/step-by-step) nor the deployment docs mention running a single instance for the first v5 boot.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Take a v4 project with published draft & publish entries (the more content, the wider the race window; a few thousand published rows are enough to make it deterministic).
2. Upgrade the project to v5.
3. Deploy so that two instances boot simultaneously against the same database, e.g. Kubernetes `replicas: 2` without a separate migration job, or locally run `npm run start` twice in parallel against the same MySQL.
4. Observe that both instances log `migrating core::5.0.0-discard-drafts` and both finish.
5. Check `strapi_migrations_internal`: migration names appear twice.
6. Check any content table: every document has two identical draft rows (`published_at IS NULL`, same `document_id`, same `locale`).

### Expected Behavior

Only one instance applies pending internal migrations. A concurrently booting instance waits for the running migration to finish or skips it. A second run of `core::5.0.0-discard-drafts` must never duplicate content.

Any single one of these would have prevented the data damage, and they compose:

1. Take a lock around the internal migration run, either Knex's own migration-lock machinery or a database advisory lock (as Rails, Flyway and Prisma do).
2. Add a unique constraint on `strapi_migrations_internal.name` and *claim* the migration (insert before running) so a concurrent runner fails fast instead of duplicating data.
3. Make `5.0.0-discard-drafts` idempotent (`NOT EXISTS` guard on the draft-clone `INSERT … SELECT`).
4. Document that the first v5 boot must run on a single instance.

### Logs

```shell
-- strapi_migrations_internal on the affected production database after the rollout.
-- Each name should appear exactly once; three appear twice.
-- discard-drafts was logged twice, 14 seconds apart: two instances, two full runs.
id | name                                        | time
 2 | 5.0.0-02-created-document-id                | 2026-08-05 05:55:25
 3 | 5.0.0-02-created-document-id                | 2026-08-05 05:55:25
 8 | core::5.0.0-discard-drafts                  | 2026-08-05 05:55:49
 9 | core::5.0.0-discard-drafts                  | 2026-08-05 05:56:03
10 | admin::migrate-prefered-language-dk-to-da   | 2026-08-05 05:56:03
11 | admin::migrate-prefered-language-dk-to-da   | 2026-08-05 05:56:03

-- Detection query used for the duplicate draft rows (per content table):
SELECT document_id, locale, COUNT(*) AS drafts
FROM <content_table>
WHERE published_at IS NULL
GROUP BY document_id, locale
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```

### Code Snippets

_No response_

### Media

_No response_

### Additional information

- This is a re-submission of #27548, which was auto-closed for not using the issue form. Content is the same, with versions corrected and the log evidence added.
- The multi-instance startup race has been reported in adjacent forms before: [forum: "Strapi database migrations on startup – race condition" (2021)](https://forum.strapi.io/t/strapi-database-migrations-on-startup-race-condition/12620) and #6697 (duplicate permissions from parallel bootstraps, 2020). As far as we can tell, the internal-migration double run with content duplication has not been reported yet.
- Workaround we shipped: the app acquires a MySQL advisory lock (`GET_LOCK`) on a dedicated pooled connection in the user `register` lifecycle and releases it at the end of `bootstrap`, so a second process waits until the first one has finished the whole boot. This works but it is application code that every multi-replica deployment would have to write itself.
- Happy to provide more detail from our incident (SQL used for detection and cleanup, invariants we checked) if useful.

### Confirmation Checklist

- [x] I have checked the existing [issues](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues) for duplicates.
- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

### Node Version

22.23.1 (also reproduced on 22.23.2)

### Package Manager

npm

### Package Manager Version

10.9.8

### Strapi Version

5.50.2

### Operating System

macOS 26.6.1 (arm64); also observed on Ubuntu

### Database

PostgreSQL 17.10

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

`Strapi.destroy()` deletes `global.strapi` and calls `process.removeAllListeners()`, but never stops the cron service. Any cron invocation still in flight at that moment rejects afterwards, and the `'error'` handler registered in `services/cron.js` dereferences the `strapi` binding that `destroy()` just deleted. **The handler itself throws `ReferenceError`**, nothing is left to catch it, and the process dies.

The practical effect: an integration suite that boots and destroys Strapi exits non-zero *after every assertion has already passed*.

Three defects compound, and the second hides the first.

**1. `destroy()` never stops cron** — `@strapi/core/dist/Strapi.js:424`:

```js
async destroy() {
  this.log.info('Shutting down Strapi');
  await this.runPluginsLifecycles(lifecycles.LIFECYCLES.DESTROY);
  for (const provider of index$7.providers) { await provider.destroy?.(this); }
  await this.runUserLifecycles(lifecycles.LIFECYCLES.DESTROY);
  await this.server.destroy();
  this.eventHub.destroy();
  await this.db?.destroy();
  process.removeAllListeners();
  delete global.strapi;
}
```

The cron service already exposes what is needed — `stop()` at `services/cron.js:73` cancels all jobs, and its `destroy()` calls `stop()`. `this.cron` is a public getter (`Strapi.js:107`). `destroy()` simply never calls either.

**2. The error handler closes over the binding `destroy()` deletes** — `services/cron.js:42`:

```js
const job = new (ns()).Job(fnWithStrapi);
job.on('error', (error) => {
  strapi.log.error(`Cron job "${taskName ?? taskExpression}" failed`, error);  // line 43
});
```

After `delete global.strapi`, `strapi` is unresolvable, so the handler throws instead of logging. Because it throws, **the underlying job failure is never reported** — you cannot learn which job failed or why.

**3. `process.removeAllListeners()`** strips the handling that might otherwise have contained the throw.

### Why stopping cron is necessary but not sufficient

`node-schedule` (2.1.1) emits `'error'` asynchronously, from a rejected promise — `lib/Invocation.js:277`:

```js
result.then(function (value) { job.emit('success', value); job.running -= 1; })
      .catch(function (err) { job.emit('error', err); job.running -= 1; });
```

`job.cancel()` unschedules future invocations but cannot retract one already running. So even a `destroy()` that stops cron first can be beaten by an invocation that started earlier and rejects later — and it *will* reject, because `destroy()` has torn down the database and server it needs.

One of Strapi's own bundled jobs makes this reliable rather than theoretical. `@strapi/upload`'s `registerCron()` schedules `uploadWeekly` at **`now + 15 seconds`** whenever no schedule is stored yet — which is always true on a fresh database (`services/weekly-metrics.js:105`):

```js
weeklySchedule = cron.getWeeklyCronScheduleAt(dateFns.add(now, { seconds: 15 }));
```

Its task performs an outbound telemetry call and then database writes, so on a fresh database any suite running longer than ~15s has a doomed invocation in flight at teardown.

Measured locally on a fresh database:

```
run started                15:17:36
uploadWeekly scheduled     15:17:54   ← boot + ~15s
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Boot Strapi against a **fresh** database: `const app = createStrapi(await compileStrapi()); await app.load()`.
2. Keep the process alive for ~20–30s (e.g. an integration suite doing real work).
3. Call `await app.destroy()`.
4. The process exits non-zero with the `ReferenceError` below, roughly 10s later, after all work succeeded.

A fresh database and a run longer than ~15s make it near-deterministic; a reused database (where `weeklySchedule` is already stored days out) will not reproduce it.

### Expected Behavior

Tearing Strapi down should be quiet, and should not be able to kill the host process.

1. `destroy()` should stop cron **before** `delete global.strapi` — e.g. `this.cron?.stop()` alongside the other teardown calls.
2. `cron.js`'s `'error'` handler should capture the logger rather than resolving `strapi` at call time, so a late rejection logs instead of throwing:

```js
const { log } = strapi;
job.on('error', (error) => {
  log.error(`Cron job "${taskName ?? taskExpression}" failed`, error);
});
```

The second change matters independently of the first: it is what makes the underlying job failure visible instead of masking it, and it is what makes a late rejection survivable in the cases point 1 cannot cover.

### Logs

```
info: Shutting down Strapi
info: Strapi has been shut down
                                         ← ~10s gap
/…/node_modules/@strapi/core/dist/services/cron.js:43
                    strapi.log.error(`Cron job "${taskName ?? taskExpression}" failed`, error);
                    ^

ReferenceError: strapi is not defined
    at Job.<anonymous> (/…/node_modules/@strapi/core/dist/services/cron.js:43:21)
    at Job.emit (node:events:519:28)
    at /…/node_modules/node-schedule/lib/Invocation.js:277:17
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:103:5)

Node.js v22.23.2
```

The suite itself was fully green — `# tests 15 | pass 14 | fail 1`, where the single failure is the test *file wrapper* recording the process's non-zero exit, not an assertion.

### Code Snippets

Teardown helper, which is enough to trigger it:

```js
const app = createStrapi(await compileStrapi())
await app.load()
// … run tests against the app …
await app.destroy()   // ← process dies ~10s later
```

### Additional information

Workaround we are using, for anyone who lands here: call `app.cron?.stop()` before `app.destroy()` in the teardown helper, and set `STRAPI_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true` in tests so the telemetry-backed jobs cannot hang on outbound requests. That removes the slow I/O holding an invocation open across teardown, but it mitigates the race rather than closing it, for the reason given above — `node-schedule` exposes no way to await in-flight invocations.

### Confirmation Checklist

- [x] I have checked the existing [issues](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues) for duplicates.
- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
items.title: [bug]: Strapi.destroy() never stops cron, and cron.js's error handler throws ReferenceError on the deleted global

### Node Version

22.22.3

### Package Manager

yarn

### Package Manager Version

1.22.22

### Strapi Version

5.40.0

### Operating System

macOS

### Database

SQLite

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

No response — the steps below are self-contained.

### Bug Description

`syncNonLocalizedAttributes` copies shared (`i18n.localized: false`) fields onto the other locales of a document. When such a field is a **component holding a relation**, the relation is resolved for the target locale through `transformData`, which is called with `allowMissingId: true`. If the related document has no entry in that locale, `getRelationIds` returns `[]` and the relation is written as `{ set: [] }`. The component rows arrive in the target locale without their relations, silently.

That state is then contagious. Because the field is shared, the next save made from that locale copies the relation-less rows back over every other locale, including the ones that still held the data. Scalar fields inside the component survive the round trip, so what an editor sees is "the rows are all there but nothing is selected" — with a 200 response and nothing in the logs.

This is not #25802 (closed as intended). Sharing a non-localized value across locales is the documented behaviour and is what we want. The defect is narrower: a relation that cannot be resolved for the target locale is written as empty instead of being left alone or raising, and that destroys the shared value for every locale.

### Steps to Reproduce

Schema:

- `api::tag.tag` — i18n + D&P, one string field.
- `api::article.article` — i18n + D&P, with a repeatable component field `blocks` carrying `pluginOptions: { i18n: { localized: false } }`. Component `shared.block` has `mode` (enumeration) and `tag` (oneToOne relation to `api::tag.tag`).
- Locales `en` (default) and `fr`.

Steps:

1. Create a tag **in `en` only** — no `fr` version.
2. Create the article in both locales.
3. Write `blocks` on the `en` article: one row, `{ mode: 'a', tag: '<tag documentId>' }`. `en` now holds the row with its relation.
4. Read the `fr` article: the row is there, `tag` is `null`. This is the silent drop — the sync could not resolve the tag in `fr`.
5. Save the `fr` article, e.g. by sending its own `blocks` array back unchanged.
6. Read the `en` article again: the row is still there and `tag` is now `null` as well. The relation is gone in every locale.

### Expected Behavior

A relation that cannot be resolved in the target locale should not be written as empty. Leaving the field untouched for that locale (ideally with a warning), raising, or linking the source locale's entry are all recoverable; silently emptying a shared field across every locale is data loss with no trace.

### Logs

```shell
# nothing — every request returns 200
```

### Code Snippets

`packages/plugins/i18n/server/src/services/localizations.ts`:

```ts
const transformedData = await strapi.documents.utils.transformData(
  cloneDeep(nonLocalizedAttributes),
  { uid, status, locale: entry.locale, allowMissingId: true }
);

const componentData = await strapi.documents(uid).updateComponents(entry, transformedData);
```

`packages/core/core/src/services/document-service/transform/relations/transform/data-ids.ts`:

```ts
if (!ids.length && !source.allowMissingId) {
  throw new errors.ValidationError(
    `Document with id "${relation.documentId}", locale "${targetLocale}" not found`
  );
}

return ids; // [] with allowMissingId -> the relation is written as { set: [] }
```

Transform output logged from inside the sync, for one locale that has the target and one that does not:

```
-> de: tag {"set":[{"id":3}]}
-> fr: tag {"set":[]}
```

### Media

_No response_

### Additional information

**Same primitive, different paths.** #26462 and #25459 both describe relations being dropped because `allowMissingId: true` turns an unresolvable id into an empty array during publish / discard-draft. This report is the i18n-sync path, which neither of them covers. `syncNonLocalizedAttributes` on `develop` still calls `transformData` with `allowMissingId: true`, still iterates locales through `async.map` with unlimited concurrency, and still has no guard, so the behaviour is present on the latest 5.x as well as on 5.40.0.

**A second, related case in the same function.** A write that creates a locale version without mentioning the shared field leaves that field empty on the new entry, and the sync then propagates the emptiness — deleting the component rows in every other locale. Related: #17563.

**Workaround** for anyone hitting this: override `strapi.plugin('i18n').service('localizations').syncNonLocalizedAttributes` so that a locale whose relations could not be resolved is skipped and logged, and a shared component whose source value is empty is not written while the target still holds rows. Comparing the relation counts before and after `transformData` is enough to detect both cases — note the relation shape changes from a populated object or array to `{ set: [...] }` across the call.

### Confirmation Checklist

- [x] I have checked the existing [issues](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues) for duplicates.
- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
items.title: [i18n] Relations inside a non-localized component are silently dropped when synced to a locale where the target does not exist

### Node Version

v24.18.0

### Package Manager

npm

### Package Manager Version

11.16.0

### Strapi Version

5.52.0

### Operating System

MacOS

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

A custom RBAC condition registered with a **custom `category`** can never have its value changed from the *Define conditions* modal. Applying the change and saving shows the "Saved" toast, but the value silently reverts: the `PUT /admin/roles/:id/permissions` request does run (the permission rows are recreated in the database), it just carries the old conditions, because the newly selected condition never makes it into the payload.

Conditions registered **without** a `category` (i.e. in the `default` category) work fine. That is what makes this easy to miss — the built-in `Is creator` / `Has same role as creator` conditions are in `default`, so they never hit it.

The cause is in `ConditionsModal.tsx`. The form state is one bucket per category, built by `createDefaultConditionsForm`:

```js
acc[categoryName] = conditionsForm;   // e.g. { default: {...}, 'My Category': {...} }
```

But every change is written into the `default` bucket only:

```js
// handleChange
draft[name].default = values;   // `values` is the full id -> boolean map for ALL categories
```

And `handleSubmit` then merges the buckets in insertion order, so the **stale** category bucket overwrites the freshly-set values:

```js
const merged = Object.values(value).reduce((acc1, current1) => ({ ...acc1, ...current1 }), {});
```

Since `default` is inserted first and the custom category last, any condition in a custom category always keeps its previous value.

A visible side effect of the same root cause: `getSelectedValues` flattens across all buckets, so a condition that is `true` in both the `default` bucket and its category bucket is counted twice — the select shows e.g. "3 currently selected" while only 2 checkboxes are ticked.

Relevant lines on `develop`: `packages/core/admin/admin/src/pages/Settings/pages/Roles/components/ConditionsModal.tsx` — `draft[name].default = values` (~L102) and the merge in `handleSubmit` (~L119). Both are unchanged as of today.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Register a custom condition with a custom `category` in `bootstrap` (see Code Snippets below).
2. Create an admin role and grant `read` on any collection type.
3. Open **Settings** on that permission, tick `My condition` under *My Category*, click **Apply**, then **Save**. A "Saved" toast appears.
4. Reload the page and reopen the modal.
5. Observe the condition is unticked, and `admin_permissions.conditions` in the database does not contain it.
6. Remove the `category` property from the condition, restart, and repeat — the condition now persists.

### Expected Behavior

A condition selected in the *Define conditions* modal is included in the payload and persisted on the permission, regardless of which category it belongs to. Custom categories should behave exactly like the `default` one.

### Code Snippets

```ts
// src/index.ts
export default {
  async bootstrap({ strapi }) {
    await strapi.service('admin::permission').conditionProvider.registerMany([
      {
        displayName: 'My condition',
        name: 'my-condition',
        plugin: 'admin',
        category: 'My Category', // <-- remove this line and it works
        handler: () => ({ slug: { $eq: 'foo' } }),
      },
    ]);
  },
};
```

### Additional information

Re-filed from #27460, which the template bot auto-closed before I could correct the formatting of the original submission.

Omitting `category` is a working workaround, at the cost of every custom condition landing under "Default".

### Confirmation Checklist

- [X] I have checked the existing [issues](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues) for duplicates.
- [X] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
items.title: Custom RBAC conditions in a custom category are silently discarded when saving a role

### Node Version

22.23.2

### Package Manager

yarn

### Package Manager Version

1.22.22

### Strapi Version

5.52.1

### Operating System

MacOS

### Database

SQLite

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

When `admin.url` is customized from `/admin` to another path, authentication cookies remain scoped to `/admin` unless `auth.cookie.path` is configured accordingly. This causes login/authentication failures because the browser does not include the cookie when requesting the customized admin URL. However, adjusting `auth.cookie.path` also changes the `Path` attribute of the refresh-token. This breaks the access token refresh mechanism because the new access token is still requested from `/admin` and not the custom `admin.url` (but now without the ill-scoped refresh token).

_Note:_ This bug is a bit difficult to reproduce outside a browser because it depends on browser cookie path scoping. Moreover, it is not clear how the login/authentication/refresh requests are intended to originate and resolve internally in Strapi. The following is my best description of the observed behavior.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `npx create-strapi@latest`
2. build app, create first user
3. add `url: "/dashboard"` to `config/admin`, rebuild admin panel, start app in production mode on localhost
4. observe that authentication fails after standard login (with `rememberMe: false`). This is because the browser does not include access token as `Authorization: Bearer` in request header. (Login with `rememberMe: true` is successful. I am not sure why.)
5. adding `auth: { cookie: { path: "/dashboard"}}` to `config/admin` changes the scope of `jwtToken` to `path: /dashboard`. Login is now successful (independent of `rememberMe`). 
6. Refresh mechanism is broken. This can be tested either by waiting 30 minutes in the browser and inspecting network logs or via suitable `curl` requests, as follows
7. ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:1337/admin/login -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"email": "your@email.com", "password": "yourpassword"}' -c cookies.txt``` returns ```< HTTP/1.1 200 OK``` and `cookies.txt` contains ```#HttpOnly_localhost	FALSE	/dashboard	FALSE	0	strapi_admin_refresh  a-string-secret-at-least-256-bits-long```
8. ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:1337/admin/access-token -b cookies.txt -v``` returns ```< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized {data:  {"message":"Missing refresh token" }}```
9. ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:1337/dashboard/access-token -b cookies.txt -v``` returns ```< HTTP/1.1 405 Method Not Allowed```
10. edit `cookies.txt` and change `Path` attribute of `strapi_admin_refresh` from `dashboard` back to `admin`
11. ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:1337/admin/access-token -b cookies.txt -v``` now returns ```< HTTP/1.1 200 OK``` and new access token in payload.

### Expected Behavior

Login/authentication and refresh should all work with custom `admin.url`. Instead, depending on details of subsequent configuration (cookie path scoping via `auth.cookie.path`) one or the other breaks. 

### Logs

```shell

```

### Code Snippets

_No response_

### Media

_No response_

### Additional information

Two recent similar issues include [26300](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/26300) and [25478](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/25478)., resolved by the [PR 26300](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/26300.)

In principle, the authentication mismatch at login can be fixed by setting `auth.cookie.path` as described above. I suspect this is intended behavior and therefore filed this as documentation issue [3384](https://github.com/strapi/documentation/issues/3384). However, the broken refresh mechanism makes it unclear whether perhaps this also is a deeper design issue or a pure documentation gap.

I might also add that in my actual production environment Strapi is served from a subpath of the NextJS frontend domain. In such reverse proxy situations, the cookie path scoping becomes even more tricky. I hope this can be taken into consideration in the fix.





### Confirmation Checklist

- [x] I have checked the existing [issues](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues) for duplicates.
- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

items.body:
### Node Version

24.14.1

### Package Manager

yarn

### Package Manager Version

4.12.0

### Strapi Version

5.52.1

### Operating System

MacOS

### Database

SQLite

### Javascript or Typescript

Javascript

### Bug Description

Every write reply from the MCP collection-type tools reports to-many relations as an empty array, whatever the document actually holds. The write itself is correct: `get_<type>` on the same document, at the same `updatedAt`, returns the relation. Only the reply is false. The reply is schema-valid (the registered output schema types the field as an array of identity objects), so nothing flags it.

This is the reply an MCP client sees immediately after its own write, so it is the reply an agent is most likely to act on: it can conclude the relation write produced an empty field and "repair" it by connecting again, or report the loss to the user. The scope is `create`, `update`, `publish`, `unpublish` and `discard_draft` on collection types. Single types are not affected, because their write handler passes an explicit populate.

Two further defects in the same relation path are filed separately: "MCP relation write accepts set and connect in one payload and silently discards connect" and "Relation write with set: null returns success and clears nothing". This issue compounds the second one, since the false `categories: []` reply agrees with the caller's wrong belief that the field was cleared.

#### What the docs say

From https://docs.strapi.io/cms/features/strapi-mcp-server (Usage > Content management through prompts > Relations, the to-many relation keys table):

> | `connect` | Add relations. Accepts an array of document ID strings or `{ documentId, locale?, status?, position? }` objects. ... |
> | `disconnect` | Remove relations. Accepts an array of document ID strings or `{ documentId, locale?, status? }` objects. |
> | `set` | Replace all existing relations with the provided array. Pass `null` to clear all relations. Mutually exclusive with `connect`/`disconnect`. |

The documented meaning of a successful `connect` is that the relation is on the document. The reply says the opposite.

#### Observed

Run on 2026-08-19 against `develop` @ `c7dbadd4feec41f0d3892c1bc9f5435e7aad3672`, instance reporting Strapi 5.52.1. Three consecutive writes, all replying `"categories":[]`, each followed or accompanied by a `get_article` read-back that returns one category:

| call | reply `categories` | `get_article` read-back |
|---|---|---|
| `update_article` with `{connect:[cat1]}` | `[]` | `[{"documentId":"xculmsrqzvdw9yfxlbhe47qb","locale":"en"}]` |
| `update_article` with `{set:[cat1], connect:[cat2]}` | `[]` | `[{"documentId":"xculmsrqzvdw9yfxlbhe47qb","locale":"en"}]` |
| `update_article` with `{set:null}` | `[]` | `[{"documentId":"xculmsrqzvdw9yfxlbhe47qb","locale":"en"}]` |

For the first row the read-back carries the same `updatedAt` as the write reply (`2026-08-19T18:50:37.881Z`), so nothing changed between the two reads. Every write reply observed in the session was false.

### Steps to Reproduce

Build tested: `strapi/strapi` `develop` @ `c7dbadd4feec41f0d3892c1bc9f5435e7aad3672` (2026-08-19), run from source with `PORT=1347 STRAPI_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true corepack yarn workspace getstarted start`, sqlite at `examples/getstarted/.tmp/data.db`, `server.mcp.enabled: true`. The instance reports 5.52.1 on node v24.14.1. The original run was on 5.52.0 @ `c43e9ee1e2`.

Setup: an Admin token with read, create and update on `api::article.article` and read and create on `api::category.category`. One category `xculmsrqzvdw9yfxlbhe47qb` and one article `b69aib6pqn0itpkibeuxot0p` with no categories yet.

1. Connect one category:

```
POST /mcp
Authorization: Bearer <admin token accessKey>
Accept: application/json, text/event-stream

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":102,"method":"tools/call","params":{
  "name":"update_article",
  "arguments":{"documentId":"b69aib6pqn0itpkibeuxot0p",
    "data":{"title":"tcref-rel-mt0g5p53",
            "categories":{"connect":["xculmsrqzvdw9yfxlbhe47qb"]}}}}}
```

`200 OK`, no `isError`, `updatedAt` `2026-08-19T18:50:37.881Z`, and the reply carries `"categories": []`.

2. Read the same document back:

```
POST /mcp
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":103,"method":"tools/call",
 "params":{"name":"get_article","arguments":{"documentId":"b69aib6pqn0itpkibeuxot0p"}}}
```

`200 OK`, same `updatedAt`, and:

```json
"categories": [{"documentId":"xculmsrqzvdw9yfxlbhe47qb","locale":"en"}]
```

The write landed. Its own reply reported the opposite.

Repeating with `set` or `disconnect`, or with `create_article` on a document that has relations, gives the same `[]`.

Re-verified on `develop` @ `c7dbadd4feec41f0d3892c1bc9f5435e7aad3672` (Strapi 5.52.1) on 2026-08-19: still reproduces, over three writes. The original 5.52.0 run recorded the same `[]` at every `update_article` reply (seven of them), with `get_article` returning the truthful identity array each time.

### Expected Behavior

A write reply reports the document's actual relations, the same identity-only array `get_<type>` returns for the same document at the same `updatedAt`. If the write path cannot cheaply produce that, the field is omitted rather than reported as empty.

### Additional information

#### Cause

The MCP collection update handler calls `documentManager.update(documentId, uid, { data, locale })` with no `populate` option (`packages/core/content-manager/server/src/mcp/handlers/collection-handlers.ts:317-325`; the populate it builds at lines 280-282 is used only for the pre-read `findOne`). `documentManager.update` then falls back to `buildDeepPopulate(uid)` (`services/document-manager.ts:100`, `services/utils/populate.ts:441-455`), which is `populateDeep(Infinity).countRelations()`, so every to-many relation comes back as `{ count: N }`, the shape the admin panel wants. `reduceToIdentity` then maps any non-array value, `{ count: N }` included, to `[]` under a comment calling it defensive: https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/c43e9ee1e20f613b63f8f10d9e52be062a8b4a72/packages/core/content-manager/server/src/mcp/sanitizers/shape-relations.ts#L73-L98 (the to-many branch is lines 79-85). Net effect: one related document is rendered as zero.

Introduced by PR #26560 (`fix(content-manager): reduce MCP relation output to identity-only shape`, commit `00da31ed44`, merged 2026-06-19). Before it the update reply carried `categories: {count: 1}`, odd but truthful. That PR added the non-array to `[]` coercion and removed `.countRelations()` only from the list and get handlers, which build their own populate; the create, update, publish, unpublish and discard_draft handlers were left on the count-shaped default. Its api tests (`tests/api/core/mcp/mcp-content-manager-shaping.test.api.ts`) cover only the get and list tools, which is why the write replies were missed. Single types are unaffected: `mcp/handlers/single-type-handlers.ts:116-118` passes an explicit populate.

Today's head still has it, byte-identical: https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/c7dbadd4feec41f0d3892c1bc9f5435e7aad3672/packages/core/content-manager/server/src/mcp/sanitizers/shape-relations.ts#L73-L98

Either fix works: pass a non-count populate from the MCP write handlers, or make `reduceToIdentity` refuse to translate `{ count: N }` into `[]`.

#### Suggested labels

`issue: bug`, `severity: high`, `source: core:content-manager`, `version: 5`

#### Related

- PR #26560 (merged 2026-06-19) introduced the misreport.
- PR #26990 (open, `feat(content-manager): add populate/fields/filters + depth guard to MCP read tools`, last pushed 2026-08-18) is actively rewriting `shape-relations.ts`, adding an inline-relation resolver and a `shouldInline` predicate, but it does not fix this: its first hunk on that file starts at line 98, so `reduceToIdentity` and its `{ count: N }` coercion at lines 83-84 are untouched context, and its `collection-handlers.ts` hunks stop well before the update handler at 317-325. If it merges as it stands, this defect survives it, so folding a fix into that PR is probably the cheapest path.
- Issue #27395 (open) is a different MCP tool-schema defect, not a duplicate.
- Searches for `mcp relation` and related phrasings found no existing report of the empty reply.

Found by TrueCourse running the product's own documentation against a live instance; the full transcript (requests, responses, server log) is available on request.

### Confirmation Checklist

items.title: MCP create and update replies report every to-many relation as an empty array

items.body:
### Node Version

24.14.1

### Package Manager

yarn

### Package Manager Version

4.12.0

### Strapi Version

5.52.1

### Operating System

MacOS

### Database

SQLite

### Javascript or Typescript

Javascript

### Bug Description

`set: null` on a to-many relation is documented as the way to clear all relations. It is a no-op that answers success: HTTP 200, no error, `updatedAt` advanced, and the relation still there afterwards. The blame is in the database package, not in MCP: `toAssocs` tests `data.set` by truthiness, so the `set` key is dropped from the payload and the write degrades into an empty partial update. Any Document Service caller passing `{ set: null }` has the same result, and has had since v4. The MCP tool schema, which accepts `null` for `set` and describes it as "null clears all", is what makes it a user-visible promise.

The asymmetry is worth stating plainly: `categories: null` does clear the relation, `categories: { set: null }` does not.

Two further defects in the same relation path are filed separately: "MCP relation write accepts set and connect in one payload and silently discards connect" (one line away in the same function) and "MCP create and update replies report every to-many relation as an empty array". The third one compounds this one: the reply to the no-op write reports `categories: []`, so the success confirmation actively agrees with the caller's wrong belief that the field is now empty.

#### What the docs say

From https://docs.strapi.io/cms/features/strapi-mcp-server (Usage > Content management through prompts > Relations, the to-many relation keys table):

> | `set` | Replace all existing relations with the provided array. Pass `null` to clear all relations. Mutually exclusive with `connect`/`disconnect`. |

#### Observed

Run on 2026-08-19 against `develop` @ `c7dbadd4feec41f0d3892c1bc9f5435e7aad3672`, instance reporting Strapi 5.52.1. Before the call, `categories` held exactly `xculmsrqzvdw9yfxlbhe47qb`.

The `set: null` call answered `200 OK`, tool result, no `isError`, and `updatedAt` advanced from `2026-08-19T18:50:37.962Z` to `2026-08-19T18:50:38.033Z`, so a write ran. The reply's own `categories` field reads `[]`. The read-back immediately after returns:

```json
"categories": [{"documentId":"xculmsrqzvdw9yfxlbhe47qb","locale":"en"}]
```

The relation survived. Nothing was logged.

### Steps to Reproduce

Build tested: `strapi/strapi` `develop` @ `c7dbadd4feec41f0d3892c1bc9f5435e7aad3672` (2026-08-19), run from source with `PORT=1347 STRAPI_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true corepack yarn workspace getstarted start`, sqlite at `examples/getstarted/.tmp/data.db`, `server.mcp.enabled: true`. The instance reports 5.52.1 on node v24.14.1. The original run was on 5.52.0 @ `c43e9ee1e2`.

Setup: an Admin token with read, create and update on `api::article.article` and read and create on `api::category.category`. One article (`b69aib6pqn0itpkibeuxot0p`) whose `categories` holds exactly one category (`xculmsrqzvdw9yfxlbhe47qb`).

1. Clear the relation the documented way:

```
POST /mcp
Authorization: Bearer <admin token accessKey>
Accept: application/json, text/event-stream

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":106,"method":"tools/call","params":{
  "name":"update_article",
  "arguments":{"documentId":"b69aib6pqn0itpkibeuxot0p",
    "data":{"title":"tcref-rel-mt0g5p53","categories":{"set":null}}}}}
```

`200 OK`, no `isError`, `updatedAt` advanced by about 70 ms.

2. Read the document back:

```
POST /mcp
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":107,"method":"tools/call",
 "params":{"name":"get_article","arguments":{"documentId":"b69aib6pqn0itpkibeuxot0p"}}}
```

`200 OK`, `categories` still holds `xculmsrqzvdw9yfxlbhe47qb`.

The same thing happens without MCP, through the Document Service API: `strapi.documents('api::article.article').update({ documentId, data: { categories: { set: null } } })` returns the document with the relation intact.

Re-verified on `develop` @ `c7dbadd4feec41f0d3892c1bc9f5435e7aad3672` (Strapi 5.52.1) on 2026-08-19: still reproduces, matching the original 5.52.0 run on every observable (200, no `isError`, `updatedAt` advancing from `15:15:31.635Z` to `15:15:31.682Z`, relation intact at the read-back).

### Expected Behavior

`{ set: null }` clears every relation on the field, as the documentation and the tool schema both state. If it is not going to clear them, the call is rejected rather than answered with a success and a bumped `updatedAt`.

### Additional information

#### Cause

`toAssocs` tests `if (data?.set)` by truthiness at line 162: https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/c43e9ee1e20f613b63f8f10d9e52be062a8b4a72/packages/core/database/src/entity-manager/index.ts#L149-L180

`{ set: null }` fails that test, falls through to the partial-update branch and becomes `{ options, connect: [], disconnect: [] }`, losing the `set` key. The consumer then cannot see the intent: `updateRelations` branches on `isNull(cleanRelationData.set)` at line 1195 for the clear-everything path, and computes `isPartialUpdate = !has('set', cleanRelationData)` at line 1198. Because the key is already gone, the write is treated as a partial update with an empty connect and an empty disconnect, so nothing is added and nothing is deleted. The null intent does survive on the other route through the same function: line 158 turns a relation value that is itself `null` into `{ set: null }`, which is why `categories: null` clears and `categories: { set: null }` does not.

The MCP layer passes the payload through untouched (`map-relation.ts:75` hands `{ set: null }` to the default visitor, which returns it unchanged), and the MCP schema correctly accepts `null` for `set`.

Introduced by `c1d82b6f9e` (2022-09-19, PR #14327, "use set format"), so this is v4-era behaviour on every Document Service caller. PR #26371 (`feat(*): introduce MCP server`, 2026-05-27) is what turned it into a broken published promise, by adding a tool schema whose `set` key accepts `z.null()` and describes it as "null clears all".

Today's head still has it, byte-identical: https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/c7dbadd4feec41f0d3892c1bc9f5435e7aad3672/packages/core/database/src/entity-manager/index.ts#L149-L180

The one-line fix is `if ('set' in data)` (or `if (data?.set !== undefined)`) instead of `if (data?.set)`. It needs regression tests rather than a straight swap: the truthiness check has been load-bearing since v4, and `set: []`, which is already truthy, is the current working way to clear a relation.

#### Suggested labels

`issue: bug`, `severity: high`, `source: core:content-manager`, `version: 5`

#### Related

- PR #14327 (merged 2022-09-30) introduced the truthiness check.
- PR #26371 (merged 2026-05-27) added the MCP schema and doc text that promise the behaviour.
- PR #27115 (open) edits the MCP relation data schema but not this path, and the fix belongs in the database package anyway.
- Issue #27395 (open) is a different MCP tool-schema defect, not a duplicate.
- Searches for `clear all relations set null` and `relation disconnect connect not working update` found no existing report.

Found by TrueCourse running the product's own documentation against a live instance; the full transcript (requests, responses, server log) is available on request.

### Confirmation Checklist

- [x] I have checked the existing [issues](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues) for duplicates.
- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

- The admin Dashboard's "Last Published Entries" widget

- Clearing browser cache
- Opening in a completely different browser (tested and confirmed same issue persists)

### Expected Behavior

The status column in the Content Manager list view should show "Published" for this entry, matching the status shown on the entry's own edit page, the Dashboard's "Last Published Entries" widget, and the REST API response.

items.body:
### Node Version

v24.18.0

### Package Manager

yarn

### Package Manager Version

4.12.0

### Strapi Version

5.52.0 (`develop`). Applies to all 5.x carrying `plugin.upload.security`.

### Operating System

Linux

### Database

Not applicable — this concerns default plugin configuration.

### Javascript or Typescript

TypeScript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

A newly created Strapi project ships with **no upload MIME restrictions at all**, so any file type is accepted until an operator configures one.

The upload plugin has a security configuration surface, `plugin.upload.security`, supporting `allowedTypes` and `deniedTypes`. The validation gate in `packages/core/upload/server/src/utils/mime-validation.ts` treats an unset `allowedTypes` as "allow everything":

```ts
if (!Array.isArray(config.allowedTypes)) {
  return { isValid: true, detectedMime: mimetype };
}
```

`packages/core/upload/server/src/config.ts` defines the plugin's defaults (`provider`, `sizeLimit`, `sharp`, concurrency) and contains **no `security` key**, so on a fresh install `allowedTypes` is `undefined` and every upload passes.

The code already recognises this as undesirable and logs at startup:

> No upload security configuration found. Consider configuring plugin.upload.security for enhanced file validation.

A warning nobody has configured against is weak protection. The default should be restrictive and widened deliberately, rather than open with a log line as the only prompt.

This is an **enhancement to our secure-by-default posture**, not a defect in the validation logic — the gate behaves as written. Filed here rather than on the feedback board because it concerns shipped defaults and has a concrete implementation shape; `blank_issues_enabled` is false and no enhancement template exists, hence the bug template.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a new project: `npx create-strapi-app@latest my-app`.
2. Start it and note the startup warning about missing upload security configuration.
3. Do not add any `plugin.upload.security` config, i.e. leave the default.
4. Upload a file of any type through the Media Library or the upload API.

Every type is accepted. `isMimeTypeAllowed` short-circuits to `true` because `allowedTypes` is not an array.

### Expected Behavior

A new project starts with a conservative `allowedTypes` covering the common media cases (images, video, audio, PDF), and an operator widens it deliberately when they need to.

Suggested shape, and the reason this is an enhancement rather than a straight fix:

- **Do not change the runtime default for existing projects.** Making `mime-validation` restrictive when unconfigured would silently break every deployment relying on today's open behaviour. That is a breaking change and should not be done quietly.
- **Ship the config in the project template instead**, so `create-strapi-app` generates a `config/plugins.*` entry with an explicit `allowedTypes`. New projects get a safe default; existing projects are untouched; the value is visible and editable rather than implicit.
- Consider promoting the startup warning to name the config path and link the docs, so existing projects have a clearer prompt.

### Logs

```
No upload security configuration found. Consider configuring plugin.upload.security for enhanced file validation.
```

### Code Snippets

Gate that short-circuits when unconfigured — `packages/core/upload/server/src/utils/mime-validation.ts`:

```ts
if (config.deniedTypes?.length && matchesMimePattern(mimetype, config.deniedTypes)) {
  return buildNotAllowedError(fileName, declaredType, detectedType, mimetype, config);
}
if (!Array.isArray(config.allowedTypes)) {
  return { isValid: true, detectedMime: mimetype };   // <- unconfigured means allow all
}
```

Plugin defaults with no `security` key — `packages/core/upload/server/src/config.ts`:

```ts
export const config = {
  default: {
    enabled: true,
    provider: 'local',
    sizeLimit: 1000000000, // 1GB
    actionOptions: {},
    sharp: { cache: false, concurrency: 1 },
    concurrentUploadSize: 1,
    concurrentUploadRequests: 1,
  },
  // no `security` key -> allowedTypes undefined -> all types accepted
};
```

### Media

_No response_

### Additional information

Docs for the validation behaviour: `docs/docs/01-core/upload/01-backend/01-mime-validation.md`.

Related: `SECURITY.md` → Testing Requirements lists "MIME type and file extension restrictions for uploads not being enforced by default" as expected behaviour requiring operator configuration. This issue does not dispute that. It proposes changing what we ship so that the operator's starting point is a safe one, which would also reduce how often the current default has to be explained.

Labelled `issue: enhancement` rather than `issue: bug`: the validation gate behaves as written, and the change requested is to the shipped defaults.

### Confirmation Checklist

- [X] I have checked the existing [issues](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues) for duplicates.
- [X] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
items.title: Ship new projects with a restrictive default upload `allowedTypes`

items.body: ### Node Version 22.23.2 ### Package Manager pnpm ### Package Manager Version 11.9.0 ### Strapi Version 5.51.2 ### Operating System Docker/Podman/LXC ### Database PostgreSQL ### Javascript or Typescript Typescript ### Reproduction URL No dedicated repository — this reproduces on a stock `npx create-strapi-app@5.51.2` project. The steps below need only one single type and two roles whose Content Manager permissions differ. ### Bug Description The admin panel fetches the current user's permissions **once per page load** and caches them for the lifetime of that page. Nothing invalidates that cache when a *new* authentication happens without a full page load, so the new session inherits the **previous user's** permissions. The token itself is replaced correctly, so requests go out as the new user and the server enforces the new user's real permissions. Only the UI is stale. The result is a panel that offers menu entries and routes the signed-in user has no access to, and every such action fails with a 403 `PolicyError`: ```json {"data":null,"error":{"status":403,"name":"PolicyError","message":"Policy Failed","details":{}}} ``` surfaced as a `Policy Failed` toast plus `Whoops! Something went wrong. Please, try again.` The most reachable path is the invite flow: an already-authenticated tab navigates to `/admin/auth/register?registrationToken=…` (the route has no guard against an active session), the invitee completes registration, and lands in the panel carrying the inviter's menu until something forces a full reload. Mechanism, in `v5.51.2`: 1. `getMyPermissions` is declared with no `providesTags`, no polling and no refetch options. Its cache key is the endpoint alone — it does not depend on the token. 2. The only reset is on logout: `clearStateAndLogout` calls `adminApi.util.resetApiState()`. 3. `login` only dispatches the token — no cache reset. The registration flow calls the same action. 4. Consumers read that cached list. For example the Content Manager filters its sidebar links through `checkUserHasPermissions`, which filters the **cached** `userPermissions`, so the menu is built for the previous user. ### Steps to Reproduce Needs two roles whose Content Manager permissions differ. Below, **Role A** can read a given single type and **Role B** cannot. 1. Fresh Strapi 5.51.2 project. Create a single type, e.g. `Featured`. 2. `Settings → Roles`: give **Role A** `Content Manager → Featured → read`; make sure **Role B** has no permission on `Featured`. 3. Log in as a Role A user through a normal page load. Confirm `Featured` is listed under **Single Types** in the Content Manager. 4. `Settings → Administration panel → Users → Invite new user`, assign **Role B**, copy the registration URL. 5. In the **same tab, without reloading**, navigate client-side to that registration URL. Any in-app navigation does it; to make the repro deterministic I used: ```js history.pushState({}, '', '/admin/auth/register?registrationToken='); dispatchEvent(new PopStateEvent('popstate')); ``` (Pasting the URL in the address bar triggers a full page load and hides the bug.) 6. Complete the registration form. You are now authenticated as the new Role B user — the server confirms `isActive: true` and `roles: [Role B]`. 7. Open the Content Manager. **`Featured` is still listed**, and the avatar still shows the previous user's initials. 8. Click `Featured` → `Policy Failed` toast and `Whoops! Something went wrong. Please, try again.`. The network tab shows `GET /content-manager/single-types/api::featured.featured` → **403** `PolicyError`. 9. Hard reload → the avatar corrects, `Featured` disappears from the menu, `SINGLE TYPES` count drops to 0. Independently verified at each step: `GET /admin/users/me/permissions` for the new user returns the correct Role B list, with no row for the single type. The server was right the whole time; only the cached client copy was wrong. ### Expected Behavior A new authentication should invalidate cached RBAC state, exactly as logout already does. Either: - have `login` (and the registration flow) dispatch `adminApi.util.resetApiState()`, mirroring `clearStateAndLogout`; or - make the permissions query depend on the authenticated identity (tag it and invalidate on token change) so it refetches instead of serving another user's list. Under no circumstance should the panel render menus, routes or ability checks from a previous user's permissions. Additionally, `/admin/auth/register` is reachable with an active session — arriving there while authenticated could reasonably clear the existing session first. ### Logs ```shell # server, request made by the freshly registered user (Role B) [2026-08-14 14:51:22.076] http: GET /content-manager/single-types/api::webinar-featured.webinar-featured (12 ms) 403 # response body {"data":null,"error":{"status":403,"name":"PolicyError","message":"Policy Failed","details":{}}} ``` ### Code Snippets `packages/core/admin/admin/src/services/auth.ts` (L41–L49) — no tags, no refetch, cache key does not include the token: ```ts getMyPermissions: builder.query({ query: () => ({ method: 'GET', url: '/admin/users/me/permissions', }), transformResponse(res: GetOwnPermissions.Response) { return res.data; }, }), ``` `packages/core/admin/admin/src/features/Auth.tsx` (L148–L149) — logout resets the cache: ```ts const clearStateAndLogout = React.useCallback(() => { dispatch(adminApi.util.resetApiState()); dispatch(logoutAction()); navigate('/auth/login'); }, [dispatch, navigate]); ``` `packages/core/admin/admin/src/features/Auth.tsx` (L288–L309) — login does not: ```ts const login = React.useCallback( async ({ rememberMe, ...body }) => { const res = await loginMutation({ ...body, deviceId: getOrCreateDeviceId(), rememberMe }); if ('data' in res) { const { token } = res.data; dispatch( loginAction({ token, persist: rememberMe, }) ); } return res; }, [dispatch, loginMutation] ); ``` `packages/core/admin/admin/src/pages/Auth/components/Register.tsx` (L337, L371) — the registration flow dispatches the same action, so it inherits the same problem: ```ts dispatch(login({ token: res.data.token })); ``` ### Media Observed during the reproduction described above: - The freshly registered Role B user's Content Manager sidebar shows `SINGLE TYPES 1`, listing the single type their role has no permission on, while the avatar still shows the previous user's initials. - Clicking that entry raises a `Policy Failed` toast over `Whoops! Something went wrong. Please, try again.`, with the underlying request returning 403 `PolicyError`. - After a hard reload, the same account shows `SINGLE TYPES 0` and the entry is gone. **1. Stale menu** — the freshly registered Role B user, still carrying the previous user's permissions: **2. The resulting failure** — clicking that entry: ### Additional information - Browser: Chrome 151.0.7922.138. Server: Strapi 5.51.2 in a Debian 12 container, PostgreSQL 16, host macOS 26.5.2. Also observed on a Kubernetes-hosted instance of the same version. - **No security impact.** The server resolves permissions per request and refuses correctly throughout; this is a client-side correctness/UX defect. The user-visible cost is that the panel advertises actions that then fail with an opaque `Policy Failed`. - Found in the wild during a QA round, where a tester reported a 403 on a content type their role legitimately cannot reach while that content type was visible in their menu. The stale cache explains both halves at once. - Untested, but the same invariant should apply to any flow where session identity changes without a page load — for example an idle tab renewing its access token from a refresh cookie that now belongs to a different account. - Duplicate search: closest existing issues are #23622 and #25131, both genuine missing-permission 403s with no stale client state involved. I found nothing covering the permission cache surviving an authentication. ### Confirmation Checklist - [x] I have checked the existing [issues](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues) for duplicates. - [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

### Node Version

### Package Manager Version

10.9.4

### Strapi Version

5.40.0

### Operating System

Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Javascript or Typescript

Javascript

### Bug Description

The maximal length of password fields seems to be checked against the plaintext password on the client side and against the password hash (alwags length 60) on the server side.

### Steps to Reproduce

- create a password field and set maximal length
- enter a password in content-manager and try to save
- see the shown warning and check network tab to see wether the warning is caused by the client- or server-side validation
- repeat with defferent maximal lengths and different password lengths

### Expected Behavior

items.body:
### Node Version

26.7.0

### Package Manager

pnpm

### Package Manager Version

10.33.0

### Strapi Version

5.52.0

### Operating System

Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)

### Database

SQLite

### Javascript or Typescript

Javascript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

`create-strapi-app` pins `better-sqlite3` to a version that does not support Node 26, while Strapi itself declares Node 26 as supported and tests against it. Installing a scaffolded SQLite application on Node 26 therefore fails outright.

The three declarations disagree:

| source | value |
|---|---|
| `packages/core/strapi/package.json` → `engines.node` | `>=20.0.0 <=26.x.x` |
| `.github/workflows/tests.yml` → CI matrix | `[22, 24, 26]` |
| `packages/cli/create-strapi-app/src/utils/database.ts:110` | `sqlite: { 'better-sqlite3': '12.8.0' }` |
| `better-sqlite3@12.8.0` → `engines.node` | `20.x \|\| 22.x \|\| 23.x \|\| 24.x \|\| 25.x` |

So Strapi advertises and CI-tests Node 26, but the default database driver it scaffolds refuses to install there.

`better-sqlite3@12.11.1` adds `26.x` to its engines range, so this looks like a pin that needs advancing rather than anything structural.

Note this is the *inverse* of the situation at the other end of the range: `engines.node` also permits Node 20, but `@strapi/utils` depends on `preferred-pm@5.0.0`, which requires `>=22.13`. So the practically installable range for 5.52.0 is 22.13 to 25.x, narrower at both ends than the declared `>=20.0.0 <=26.x.x`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Node 26 (26.7.0 used here).
2. Scaffold a new application, choosing **SQLite** as the database — or add `"better-sqlite3": "12.8.0"` to an existing project, which is what `create-strapi-app` writes.
3. Install dependencies.

The install aborts on the engine check. npm reports the same incompatibility as a warning by default rather than an error, but the underlying constraint is identical and the native module has no Node 26 prebuild.

### Expected Behavior

A database option offered by `create-strapi-app` should install on every Node version Strapi declares support for.

Either:

- advance the `better-sqlite3` pin to a release whose engines include `26.x` (`12.11.1` or later), or
- narrow `engines.node` in `packages/core/strapi/package.json` so it does not claim support for a version the default scaffold cannot install on.

The first seems preferable given CI already runs on Node 26.

### Logs

```shell
error better-sqlite3@12.8.0: The engine "node" is incompatible with this module. Expected version "20.x || 22.x || 23.x || 24.x || 25.x". Got "26.7.0"
error Found incompatible module.
```

### Code Snippets

`packages/cli/create-strapi-app/src/utils/database.ts`

```ts
const clientDependencies = {
  // ...
  sqlite: { 'better-sqlite3': '12.8.0' },
};
```

`packages/core/strapi/package.json`

```json
{
  "engines": {
    "node": ">=20.0.0 <=26.x.x",
    "npm": ">=6.0.0"
  }
}
```

### Media

_No response_

### Additional information

Encountered while extending the CI matrix of `@strapi-community/plugin-rest-cache` to match Strapi's own `[22, 24, 26]`. The plugin's test applications are ordinary Strapi apps using SQLite, and the Node 26 leg failed at install for this reason while 22 and 24 passed. Moving the pin to `better-sqlite3@12.11.1` resolved it with no other change.

### Confirmation Checklist

- [X] I have checked the existing [issues](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues) for duplicates.
- [X] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

### Node Version

22.23.2

### Package Manager

yarn

### Package Manager Version

4.12.0

### Strapi Version

5.51.2

### Operating System

MacOS

### Database

SQLite

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

https://github.com/strapi/strapi

### Bug Description

Strapi's published type definitions are not compatible with TypeScript's [`exactOptionalPropertyTypes`](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/#exactOptionalPropertyTypes) compiler flag.

With `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`, an optional property declared as `prop?: T` no longer accepts an explicit `undefined` value — `undefined` has to be part of the declared type (`prop?: T | undefined`). Strapi's types declare optional properties with `?` alone while still expecting consumers to be able to pass `undefined` (for example when spreading partially-populated objects or forwarding optional variables into Document Service calls). Any project that enables the flag therefore gets type errors it cannot fix without patching Strapi's `.d.ts` files.

> [!NOTE]
> This report is based on a [generic issue template](https://gist.github.com/unrevised6419/8bdfca183fde610708685a60c2510b1e) used to raise awareness about `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` support across TypeScript libraries.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a Strapi project with TypeScript (`npx create-strapi-app@latest my-project --typescript`).
2. Enable the flag in `tsconfig.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "compilerOptions": {
       "exactOptionalPropertyTypes": true
     }
   }
   ```
3. Write code that assigns `undefined` to an optional property of a Strapi-provided type, or forwards a possibly-`undefined` variable into a Strapi API (for example a Document Service call, plugin config object, or a `@strapi/types` structure).
4. Run `npx tsc --noEmit`.
5. Observe errors of the form `Type 'undefined' is not assignable to type 'X' with 'exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true'. Consider adding 'undefined' to the type of the target.`

### Expected Behavior

Type-checking succeeds with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`.

Optional properties in Strapi's public types should declare `| undefined` explicitly wherever passing an explicit `undefined` is a supported usage, so that consumers on stricter TypeScript settings can use Strapi without patching its type definitions.

### Logs

```shell
error TS2375: Type '{ config: undefined; }' is not assignable to type 'Example' with 'exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true'. Consider adding 'undefined' to the types of the target's properties.
  Types of property 'config' are incompatible.
    Type 'undefined' is not assignable to type 'SomeConfig'.
```

### Code Snippets

Current behavior:

```ts
// Type from this library
type Example = {
  config?: SomeConfig;
};

// Usage
const x: Example = {
  config: undefined, // ❌ Error with exactOptionalPropertyTypes
};
```

Expected:

```ts
// Explicitly allow undefined where it is a supported value
type Example = {
  config?: SomeConfig | undefined;
};
```

### Additional information

This is a re-file of [#23480](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/23480), which was closed by automation for not following the bug report template. The report now follows the template.

#### Suggested fix

Audit the type definitions and add `| undefined` where an explicit `undefined` is intentional.

#### Reasoning about optional properties

**Use only `?` (e.g. `prop?: T`)**

- Use when the property can be **omitted entirely**.
- Do **not** expect consumers to explicitly pass `undefined`.
- Example: config objects where the value is optional and can be left out.

```ts
type Options = {
  retry?: boolean;
};
```

**Use only `| undefined` (e.g. `prop: T | undefined`)**

- Use when the property is required to exist but the value may be `undefined`.
- Useful when the property is always present, but its value is unset or to be determined later.

```ts
type Response = {
  data: string | undefined; // must exist, but may be undefined
};
```

**Use both `?: T | undefined`**

- Use when the property is optional and may explicitly be set to `undefined`.
- Required if consumers may want to pass `undefined` explicitly to override a default or signal absence.

```ts
type Config = {
  timeout?: number | undefined;
};
```

#### Suggestion for library authors

To proactively avoid these issues and align with modern TypeScript practices, consider enabling the `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` flag in Strapi's own `tsconfig.json`. This helps:

- Enforce more **accurate typing** of optional properties
- Prevent **unintentional `undefined` assignments**
- Improve type safety for consumers using strict settings
- Catch inconsistencies early during development

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "exactOptionalPropertyTypes": true
  }
}
```

Adopting this flag now ensures the types remain robust and future-proof as more of the ecosystem adopts stricter settings.

#### References

- [TypeScript 4.4 release notes](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-4-4.html#exact-optional-property-types)

#### Support in other packages

- ✅ [Vue](https://github.com/vuejs/core/pull/12771)
- ✅ [React](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/blob/master/types/react/index.d.ts)
- ✅ [Ember](https://github.com/tildeio/router.js/pull/339)
- ✅ [Base UI](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/pull/3302)
- ✅ [Material UI](https://github.com/mui/material-ui/pull/47750)
- ✅ [Prisma](https://github.com/prisma/prisma/issues/20169)
- ✅ [Floating UI](https://github.com/floating-ui/floating-ui/pull/3456)
- ✅ [Zod](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/1510)
- ✅ [React Router](https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/issues/10392#issuecomment-4803469947)
- ⚠️ [TypeScript ESLint](https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/issues/6307)
- ⚠️ [Headless UI](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/headlessui/issues/3388)
- ⚠️ [AWS CDK](https://github.com/aws/aws-cdk/discussions/23885)
- ⚠️ [RadixVue/RekaUI](https://github.com/unovue/reka-ui/issues/1404)
- ⚠️ [RadixUI](https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives/issues/3535)
- ⚠️ [Strapi](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/23480)
- ⚠️ [Strapi Design System](https://github.com/strapi/design-system/issues/2045)

Not many libraries support this today, and a lot more do not — it would be great to see that change.

[![thumbnail](https://i3.ytimg.com/vi/krj9KCxJ5OY/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/krj9KCxJ5OY?t=162)
