### Node Version

20.x (not version-dependent — admin panel React state)

### Package Manager

npm

### Package Manager Version

10.x

### Strapi Version

5.51.2 (present since 5.26.0)

### Operating System

Other

### Database

SQLite

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Bug Description

The AI credit usage notification re-appears on every full page load of the admin panel, even after the user has dismissed it. Users at or above their AI credit threshold see the same banner again on every refresh, indefinitely.

The notification's "already shown at this level" state is held in a React `useRef`, which is reinitialised on every mount. There is no persistence — no `localStorage`, no `sessionStorage`, no server-side acknowledgement — so a full page load always re-evaluates from an empty set and fires the notification again.

`packages/core/admin/ee/admin/src/hooks/useAIUsageWarning.ts:23`

```ts
const warningLevelsRef = useRef(new Set<number>());
```

`useGetAiUsageQuery` is also configured with `refetchOnMountOrArgChange: true` (line 20), so usage is refetched and re-evaluated on every load.

The dedupe works as intended *within* a single SPA session — client-side route changes do not re-fire it — but it cannot survive a page reload.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a project with Strapi AI enabled and an AI credit allowance.
2. Consume at least 80% of the monthly AI credit allowance, so that `cmsAiCreditsUsed / cmsAiCreditsBase >= 0.8`.
3. Load the admin panel. The AI credit usage notification appears.
4. Dismiss it, or wait for it to auto-dismiss after its 5s timeout.
5. Navigate between routes inside the admin panel. The notification correctly does **not** re-appear.
6. Reload the page.

Observed: the notification appears again, and re-appears on every subsequent reload.

### Expected Behavior

Once a user has been notified about crossing a given AI usage threshold (80%, 90%, 100%), they should not be re-notified for that threshold within the same billing period, regardless of page reloads.

The notification should re-arm when a new threshold is crossed, or when the billing period resets.

### Logs

```shell
n/a - client-side only, no error is emitted
```

### Code Snippets

```ts
// packages/core/admin/ee/admin/src/hooks/useAIUsageWarning.ts
const warningLevelsRef = useRef(new Set<number>());   // resets on every mount

// ...
if (percentUsed >= 1 && !warningLevelsRef.current.has(100)) {
  toggleNotification({
    type: 'danger',
    message: `You've used 100% of your AI credits. Overages are being applied.`,
    timeout: 5000,
  });
  warningLevelsRef.current.add(100);
}
```

### Additional information

Internal ticket: Pylon 9462

Identified by source inspection rather than a runtime reproduction; the mechanism is deterministic from the code.

Suggested fix: persist the warned-threshold set per user and billing period — `localStorage` keyed on user id + period, or a server-side acknowledgement — instead of a `useRef`. The existing reset condition (`percentUsed < 0.7` clears the set) would need to survive the same way.

There is no test coverage for the reload/remount case: `packages/core/admin/ee/admin/src/hooks/tests/useAIUsageWarning.test.tsx` contains no reference to persistence, reload or remount. A regression test should go in with the fix.

Introduced in v5.26.0 (#23730), unchanged through v5.51.2.

- [X] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

> You should never use this command to run a Strapi application in production.

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

When a user's role has locale permissions restricted so they cannot access a content type's
default locale, simply landing on that content type with **no locale specified in the URL**
(e.g. clicking it in the Content Manager sidebar) crashes with a raw `403 Forbidden` and a
generic error screen, instead of the friendly "you don't have permission for this locale"
message and automatic redirect to an accessible locale.

By contrast, explicitly switching to a disallowed locale via the URL (e.g. adding
`?plugins[i18n][locale]=en`) **does** show the correct message and redirects to an accessible
locale — so the default-locale-resolution code path (triggered simply by landing on the page
with no locale param) does not get the same handling as the explicit-locale-switch path.

Found while manually QA-testing PR #27146 ("fix: Handle i18n conflict and local rights",
linked issue #26707) for release 5.51.2 — that PR's own documented test steps (explicit locale
switch) pass; this is a distinct gap reached via a different, more common entry point.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Add a second locale to a Strapi project (e.g. `fr`, alongside the default `en`).
2. Enable i18n localization on a content type (`pluginOptions.i18n.localized: true`), with
   content created in both locales.
3. Create a role whose locale permissions for that content type are restricted to the
   non-default locale only (e.g. `fr` allowed, `en` — the content type's default — not
   allowed).
4. Log in as a user with that role.
5. Navigate directly to the content type with no locale specified in the URL — e.g. click it
   in the Content Manager sidebar, or go to
   `/admin/content-manager/single-types/<uid>` with no `?plugins[i18n][locale]=` query param.

### Expected Behavior

The same graceful handling that already exists for the explicit-locale-switch case: a clear
"you don't have permission for this locale" message, and an automatic redirect to a locale the
user can access.

### Logs

```
GET /content-manager/single-types/api::about.about -> 403
{"data":null,"error":{"status":403,"name":"ForbiddenError","message":"Forbidden","details":{}}}
```

### Code Snippets

```json
// About singleType schema — pluginOptions used to reproduce
{
  "kind": "singleType",
  "pluginOptions": {
    "i18n": { "localized": true }
  }
}
```

### Media

UI shows a "Forbidden" toast plus a generic full-panel error state: "Whoops! Something went
wrong. Please, try again." — no locale-specific messaging, no redirect.

### Additional information

- Reproduced twice, in two separate, fresh browser sessions with a freshly logged-in user —
  not a one-off flake.
- Also reproducible from a plain `create-strapi-app` scaffold with only a second locale added
  and i18n enabled on one content type.

Selecting an **existing** relation from the same combobox (no creation) works with no error,
so this is isolated specifically to the on-the-fly relation-*creation* flow when the relation
field is nested inside a dynamic-zone component.

Found while manually QA-testing PR #27081 ("fix(content-manager): relation creation discards
parent changes", linked issue #24933) for release 5.51.2 — that PR's own fix (preserving
parent form data when a relation is added inside a DZ component) works correctly and is not
implicated here; this is a separate, pre-existing issue in the relation-creation UI itself.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On a content type with a dynamic zone field, add a component to the dynamic zone that has
   a relation attribute (e.g. a `relatedCategory` relation field on a `shared.quote`
   component, targeting any collection type).
2. In the new component's relation field, type a name that does not match any existing
   related entry.
3. Click **"Create a relation"** in the dropdown (the on-the-fly creation option).

### Expected Behavior

The "Create a relation" modal should open cleanly, ready for input (optionally pre-filled with
the typed search text), with no error.

### Logs

```
An error occurred while trying to add the relation.

You've tried to add a relation with an id that does not exist in the options you can see,
this is likely a bug with Strapi. Please open an issue.
```

### Code Snippets

```json
// src/components/shared/quote.json (relation field added inside a DZ component to reproduce)
{
  "collectionName": "components_shared_quotes",
  "info": { "displayName": "Quote", "icon": "indent" },
  "options": {},
  "attributes": {
    "title": { "type": "string" },
    "body": { "type": "text" },
    "relatedCategory": {
      "type": "relation",
      "relation": "manyToMany",
      "target": "api::category.category"
    }
  }
}
```

### Media

Error toast fires the instant the create-modal opens, before any user input. The modal's
`name` field also does not get pre-filled with the text typed in the combobox, and clicking
**Save** afterward does not appear to close or persist the modal (title stays "Untitled").

### Additional information

- Filling in the modal's `name` field manually and clicking **Save** does not close the modal
  or visibly save.
- Reproduced twice, in two separate, fresh browser sessions — not a one-off flake.
- Also reproducible from a plain `create-strapi-app` scaffold with no other customization
  beyond adding the relation field above.

### Node Version

24.18.0

### Package Manager

pnpm

### Package Manager Version

11.15.1

### Strapi Version

5.51.1

### Operating System

Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)

### Database

MariaDB

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

When an ordered relation changes, `@strapi/database` re-numbers the join table's order column via `cleanOrderColumns`. On MySQL/MariaDB it issues a **multi-table `UPDATE` joined to a derived table** that contains a `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY …)` window function.

A **MariaDB Galera Cluster** cannot build a replication write-set for that statement shape and rejects it outright:

```
errno:      4165
sqlState:   HY000
sqlMessage: Galera replication not supported
```

The result: **any write that touches an ordered relation fails** on a Galera-backed database — e.g. reassigning a `manyToOne` relation, or reordering a `manyToMany`/`oneToMany` list. 

This is deterministic and tied to the statement *shape* — it is not a concurrency/certification (deadlock) issue.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Stand up a MariaDB **Galera Cluster** with `wsrep`/`pxc_strict_mode` enabled (the default enforcing mode).
2. Create two collection types with a **bidirectional relation that has an order column** — e.g. `manyToOne` with `inversedBy` (or a `manyToMany`). This produces a `_lnk` join table with an order column (`*_ord`).
3. Point Strapi at the cluster (`DATABASE_CLIENT=mysql`) and start it.
4. Create a few entries and link several of them to the same target.
5. Change/reassign the relation (or reorder the list) via the admin panel or the Document/Entity Service.

**Result:** the request 500s; the server log shows errno 4165 / "Galera replication not supported" for a query like the one below.

### Expected Behavior

Order-column maintenance should use a statement shape that replicates on Galera-family clusters (as it already must for correctness under row-based replication). The order values should remain contiguous per partition, exactly as today.


### The failing query

Generated by `cleanOrderColumns` → `updateInverseOrderColumn` (the `updateOrderColumn` variant is identical with `src_order`):

```sql
UPDATE `akamai_properties_project_lnk` as a, (
  select `id`,
         row_number() over (partition by `project_id` order by `akamai_property_ord`) as inv_order
  from `akamai_properties_project_lnk`
  where `project_id` in (35)
) AS b
SET `akamai_property_ord` = b.inv_order
WHERE b.id = a.id
```

(Table/column names are from our project; the shape is generic to any ordered relation.)

### Code pointers

`packages/core/database/src/entity-manager/regular-relations.ts`, function `cleanOrderColumns`:

- `updateOrderColumn` — `case 'mysql'`: `UPDATE ?? as a, ( <select with ROW_NUMBER()> ) AS b SET ?? = b.src_order WHERE b.id = a.id`
- `updateInverseOrderColumn` — `case 'mysql'`: same shape with `b.inv_order`

Note the `default:` (Postgres) branch already uses a **single-target-table** form (`UPDATE ?? as a SET … FROM ( <select> ) AS b WHERE …`), which is why Postgres is unaffected. Only the MySQL/MariaDB branch uses the multi-table-target form that Galera rejects.

### Proposed fix

Keep the exact `ROW_NUMBER()` semantics, but compute the ranking in JS and apply it as a **single-table** `UPDATE … SET col = CASE id WHEN … THEN … END WHERE id IN (…)`. Single target table, PK-keyed, deterministic → replicates cleanly under Galera's row-based replication. No new dependencies.

`updateOrderColumn` (MySQL branch):

```ts
case 'mysql': {
  // Galera (MariaDB wsrep) rejects the multi-table UPDATE + derived-table form
  // with errno 4165. Reproduce ROW_NUMBER() app-side and apply as a single-table UPDATE.
  const rows = await db
    .connection(joinTable.name)
    .select('id')
    .where(joinColumn.name, id)
    .orderBy([{ column: orderColumnName }, { column: 'id' }])
    .transacting(trx);

  if (rows.length > 0) {
    const ids = rows.map((r) => r.id);
    const cases = ids.map((_, i) => `WHEN ? THEN ${i + 1}`).join(' ');
    const placeholders = ids.map(() => '?').join(', ');
    await db
      .getConnection()
      .raw(`UPDATE ?? SET ?? = CASE id ${cases} END WHERE id IN (${placeholders})`, [
        joinTable.name,
        orderColumnName,
        ...ids,
        ...ids,
      ])
      .transacting(trx);
  }
  break;
}
```

`updateInverseOrderColumn` (MySQL branch) is the same, but ranks reset **per partition** (`inverseJoinColumn`) to mirror `PARTITION BY`:

```ts
case 'mysql': {
  const rows = await db
    .connection(joinTable.name)
    .select('id', inverseJoinColumn.name)
    .where(inverseJoinColumn.name, 'in', inverseRelIds)
    .orderBy([
      { column: inverseJoinColumn.name },
      { column: inverseOrderColumnName },
      { column: 'id' },
    ])
    .transacting(trx);

  if (rows.length > 0) {
    const counters = new Map<unknown, number>();
    const ranked = rows.map((r) => {
      const partition = r[inverseJoinColumn.name];
      const next = (counters.get(partition) ?? 0) + 1;
      counters.set(partition, next);
      return { id: r.id, order: next };
    });
    const ids = ranked.map((r) => r.id);
    const cases = ranked.map((r) => `WHEN ? THEN ${r.order}`).join(' ');
    const placeholders = ids.map(() => '?').join(', ');
    await db
      .getConnection()
      .raw(`UPDATE ?? SET ?? = CASE id ${cases} END WHERE id IN (${placeholders})`, [
        joinTable.name,
        inverseOrderColumnName,
        ...ids,
        ...ids,
      ])
      .transacting(trx);
  }
  break;
}
```

The ranks are integers computed in code (safe to inline); all ids are parameterized. Order lists are small, so the extra `SELECT` is negligible. Happy to open a PR.

### Logs

```shell
Error: UPDATE `properties_project_lnk` as a, ( select `id`, row_number() over (partition by `project_id` order by `property_ord`) as inv_order from `properties_project_lnk` where `project_id` in (35) ) AS b
            SET `property_ord` = b.inv_order
            WHERE b.id = a.id - Galera replication not supported
    at Packet.asError (/opt/node_modules/mysql2/lib/packets/packet.js:728:17)
    at Query.execute (/opt/node_modules/mysql2/lib/commands/command.js:29:26)
    at Connection.handlePacket (/opt/node_modules/mysql2/lib/connection.js:481:34)
    at PacketParser.onPacket (/opt/node_modules/mysql2/lib/connection.js:97:12)
    at PacketParser.executeStart (/opt/node_modules/mysql2/lib/packet_parser.js:75:16)
    at Socket.<anonymous> (/opt/node_modules/mysql2/lib/connection.js:104:25)
    at Socket.emit (node:events:519:28)
    at Socket.emit (node:domain:489:12)
    at addChunk (node:internal/streams/readable:561:12)
    at readableAddChunkPushByteMode (node:internal/streams/readable:512:3)
{
  "errno": 4165,
  "sql": "UPDATE `properties_project_lnk` as a, ( select `id`, row_number() over (partition by `project_id` order by `property_ord`) as inv_order from `properties_project_lnk` where `project_id` in (35) ) AS b\n            SET `property_ord` = b.inv_order\n            WHERE b.id = a.id",
  "sqlMessage": "Galera replication not supported",
  "sqlState": "HY000"
}
```

### Bug Description

Setting a non-English admin interface language (tested with `fr`) does not translate
the admin UI. The locale is correctly persisted (`localStorage["strapi-admin-language"] = "fr"`,
and `user.preferedLanguage = "fr"` via `PUT /admin/users/me`), and locale-aware formatting
(e.g. relative timestamps like "il y a 2 heures") correctly reflects French. However, static
UI strings (buttons, menus, labels) remain in English everywhere.

Network inspection shows the corresponding `fr.json-*.js` translation chunk is **never
fetched** by the browser, even though:
- The chunk exists in the production build output (`dist/build/fr.json-*.js`)
- The bundle contains a working dynamic-import switch for it
  (`case "./translations/fr.json": return import("./fr.json-XXXX.js")`)
- The redux/localStorage locale state is correctly `"fr"` throughout

Only the `en.json-*.js` chunks are ever requested, and the login-page language picker
(`Select interface language`) only ever lists **"English"** as an option, even though
`languageNativeNames.js` includes `fr: 'Français'` and dozens of other locales.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Fresh Strapi 5.51.1 project (`create-strapi-app`, TypeScript, SQLite in local dev → migrated to PostgreSQL for production), default admin i18n setup, no custom `config/admin.ts` locale settings.
2. Run `strapi build && strapi start` in production mode.
3. Log in, go to Profile, or call `PUT /admin/users/me` with `{"preferedLanguage":"fr"}`.
4. Reload the admin panel.
5. Observe: UI stays in English; open the Network tab — no `fr.json-*.js` request is ever made.
6. Open the login page's language dropdown (top-right) — only "English" is listed as a selectable option.

### Expected Behavior

- The login-page language dropdown should list all bundled locales (matching `languageNativeNames.js`).
- Setting `preferedLanguage` (or selecting a language from the picker) should trigger loading of the matching translation chunk and translate the UI.

### Additional information

This was originally reported in #27167 and #27170, which were auto-closed by the issue-template bot for not matching the structured form (the information was present, just not under the exact expected headers). Re-filing with the form fields filled in correctly this time.

### Node Version

22.23.1

### Package Manager

npm

### Package Manager Version

11.18.0

### Strapi Version

5.51.0

### Operating System

Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)

### Database

MariaDB

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

The auto-exclude heuristic added in #26944 (react peer + ESM export condition + pre-built `dist/`) matches `@_sh/strapi-plugin-ckeditor` and puts it in `optimizeDeps.exclude`. That plugin wraps the large `ckeditor5` package tree (~180 packages). Once excluded, Vite's scanner never opens *any* of it — so every CJS-only leaf dependency anywhere in that tree gets served raw/unbundled and fails native ESM interop.

This is the same bug class already fixed reactively in #27014 for `invariant` — but that fix only pins `invariant` and protects `@strapi/*` from ever being excluded. It does nothing for third-party plugins that get excluded and happen to depend (transitively, often several levels deep) on old-style CJS packages.

### Confirmed breaks

Found by walking the full dependency graph of the excluded plugin (184 packages, BFS from `@_sh/strapi-plugin-ckeditor`):

| Package | Reached via | Error |
|---|---|---|
| `property-expr` | `yup` (`Reference.js`: `import { getter } from 'property-expr'`) | `does not provide an export named 'getter'` |
| `fuzzysort` | `@ckeditor/ckeditor5-emoji` | `does not provide an export named 'default'` |
| `es-toolkit/compat` | `ckbox`/`core`/`clipboard`/... (barrel import) | same |
| `es-toolkit/compat/isEqual` | `@ckeditor/ckeditor5-image` (deep single-file import, separate specifier from the barrel above) | same |
| `color-convert` | `@ckeditor/ckeditor5-ui` (color picker) | same |
| `extend` | `unified` (`lib/index.js:350`, via `ckeditor5-markdown-gfm`) | same |
| `escape-string-regexp` | `mdast-util-find-and-replace` → `mdast-util-newline-to-break` → `remark-breaks` | same |
| `debug` | `micromark` (dev build) → `mdast-util-from-markdown` → `remark-parse` | same, `browser.js` |

Every one of these is a plain "no `type: module`, no `module` field, no `exports.import` condition" CJS package — i.e. exactly the shape #27014 already identified as broken by this heuristic, just recurring per-package instead of being handled generically.

### Why this matters beyond our case

The heuristic's match criteria (react peer + ESM export condition + `dist/`) is common for *any* well-packaged Strapi plugin today, not just UI-kit singletons. Any plugin wrapping a large third-party library (rich text editors, chart libs, etc.) is likely to hit the same cascade.

### Suggested direction

Rather than patching one leaf package at a time (as #27014 did for `invariant`), when a package is added to `optimizeDeps.exclude` by this heuristic, its transitive dependency tree should still be crawled for CJS-only leaves and those force-included — or the heuristic should be scoped to actual shared singletons rather than "anything with a react peer + dist + ESM condition."

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Strapi 5.51.0, admin plugin with a React peer dep, ESM export condition, pre-built `dist/` (e.g. `@_sh/strapi-plugin-ckeditor`) that wraps a large third-party library with old-style CJS dependencies.
2. `strapi develop`, open `/admin`, navigate through the plugin's features (emoji picker, color picker, markdown paste, etc.).
3. Console errors accumulate one at a time, each a different `SyntaxError: ... does not provide an export named ...`, as different code paths through the plugin get exercised.

### Expected Behavior

Excluding a plugin from optimizeDeps shouldn't silently drop pre-bundling for that plugin's own transitive CJS dependencies. Either:
- crawl excluded packages' own imports and still pre-bundle those, or
- widen the invariant-style safety net (optimizeDeps.include) to cover other commonly-transitive CJS packages (yup, property-expr, etc.), or
- scope the exclude heuristic to skip packages whose bundle imports anything outside the "singleton" set.

### Logs

```shell

```

### Code Snippets

### Workaround

Project's `src/admin/vite.config.ts`:

```ts
optimizeDeps: {
  include: [
    'yup', 'property-expr', 'fuzzysort',
    'es-toolkit', 'es-toolkit/compat', 'es-toolkit/compat/isEqual',
    'color-convert', 'extend', 'escape-string-regexp', 'debug',
  ],
}
```

Confirmed working for each entry (checked the generated `.strapi/vite/deps/_metadata.json` chunk for a real `default`/named export after each addition) — but this list grows every time a different part of the plugin's UI is exercised, and required manually walking `node_modules` to find each one.

### Operating System

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/25873

### Bug Description

After the TypeScript 6 bump ([#25873](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/25873)), the monorepo does not yet exercise `--stableTypeOrdering`.

TypeScript 6 introduced `stableTypeOrdering` so that type/union/property ordering matches TypeScript 7’s algorithm ([TS 6.0 notes](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-6-0.html#the---stabletypeordering-flag)). Without it, declaration emit and rare inference results can still depend on encounter order — differences that become hard failures or noisy `.d.ts` churn under TS7.

Shared presets (`packages/utils/tsconfig/base.json`, `client.json`) currently set TS6 options (`moduleResolution: Bundler`, `erasableSyntaxOnly`, etc.) but leave `stableTypeOrdering` unset (defaults to `false`).

Raised on the PR by [@unrevised6419](https://github.com/unrevised6419): [comment](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/25873#issuecomment-4918817950).

This is an internal monorepo readiness check, not a runtime Strapi application bug.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out `strapi/strapi` on `chore/typescript-6` (or `develop` once [#25873](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/25873) lands) with `typescript@6.0.2`.
2. Enable the flag on the shared base (and client if needed), e.g. in `packages/utils/tsconfig/base.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "stableTypeOrdering": true
  }
}
```

3. From the repo root, run the usual typecheck / build:types path used in CI (`yarn test:ts` and/or `yarn build`).
4. Observe whether type errors appear (typically inference that relied on previous type-ID ordering) and whether `.d.ts` emit order changes.

### Expected Behavior

- `yarn test:ts` / `yarn build` succeed with `stableTypeOrdering: true`, or any failures are fixed with explicit type arguments / annotations (the recommended TS6→TS7 remediation).
- Decision recorded: keep the flag temporarily as a TS7 gate, or run it as a one-off validation and leave it off (Microsoft notes it can slow type-checking by up to ~25% and is not meant as a long-term default).

### Logs

```shell
# Not run yet — validation pending after #25873 is green.
# Expected failure shape (from TS docs): inference / assignability errors
# that disappear when an explicit type argument or annotation is added.
```

### Code Snippets

Current shared base (`packages/utils/tsconfig/base.json`) — no `stableTypeOrdering`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "Bundler",
    "noUncheckedSideEffectImports": true,
    "erasableSyntaxOnly": true,
    "types": ["node"]
  }
}
```

### Media

_No response_

### Additional information

- Source comment: https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/25873#issuecomment-4918817950
- Related: [#25861](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/25861) (TS7 / `moduleResolution: node`), PR [#25873](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/25873) (TS 6 bump)
- Docs: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-6-0.html#the---stabletypeordering-flag
- Prefer not to land `stableTypeOrdering: true` permanently until cost vs signal is measured on this monorepo.

### Confirmation Checklist

- [x] I have checked the existing [issues](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues) for duplicates.
- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

---

### Node Version

24.18.0

### Package Manager

yarn

### Package Manager Version

4.15.0

### Strapi Version

5.50.1

### Operating System

Linux (Other)

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

 Bug:
  When an admin user duplicates a collection-type entry and their role lacks field-level permission for all nested attributes of a non-repeatable component field, Content Manager can create an empty
  component row instead of preserving the source component or omitting the component.

  Generic example:
  A collection type has a non-repeatable component field:

  - `metadata`
  - component UID: `shared.metadata`
  - component attributes: `label`, `score`, `notes`

  A restricted admin role can create/read/update the parent collection type, but cannot access:

  - `metadata.label`
  - `metadata.score`
  - `metadata.notes`

  When that user duplicates an entry, the admin UI does not include `metadata` in the clone request body. However, the server-side clone sanitizer can synthesize:

  ```json
  {
    "metadata": {
      "label": null,
      "score": null,
      "notes": null
    }
  }
```

  That all-null component payload overwrites the source component during clone and causes Strapi to insert an empty component row.

  Root cause:
  The clone controller sanitizes ctx.request.body, then runs clone-specific field exclusion, then calls the document manager clone path.

  The issue appears to be in Content Manager clone sanitization, likely around:

  packages/core/content-manager/server/src/controllers/utils/clone.ts

### Steps to Reproduce

  1. Create a collection type, for example `Article`.

  2. Add a non-repeatable component field to it, for example:
     - field name: `metadata`
     - component UID: `shared.metadata`
     - attributes: `label`, `score`, `notes`

  3. Create an entry of that collection type without setting the `metadata` component.

  4. Create or update an admin role that can create/read/update the parent collection type, but does not have field-level permission for any nested component fields:
     - `metadata.label`
     - `metadata.score`
     - `metadata.notes`

  5. Log in to the admin panel as a user with that restricted role.

  6. Open the existing entry and use the Content Manager `Duplicate` action.

  7. Save/create the duplicated entry.

  8. Inspect the database component table and component join table.

### Expected Behavior

A component field omitted from the clone request because the user cannot access its nested fields should not be materialized as { nestedField: null }.

  For clone, omission should mean “leave the source value alone during clone merge”, not “create an empty component”.

  Fix direction:
  Update clone field-exclusion logic so it does not create missing component objects when recursing into inaccessible nested fields.

### Node Version

_No response_

### Bug Description

When a collection type has i18n enabled and contains a localized repeatable component (pluginOptions.i18n.localized: true on the component field), querying an entry in a non-default locale via GraphQL returns the component data from the DEFAULT locale, not the requested one.

What isolates it to the GraphQL layer:
- Localized scalar fields on the same entry return correctly for the requested locale.
- The REST API returns the component correctly for the requested locale — the data is stored per-locale fine.
- Same wrong result whether fetched by filters or by documentId.








### Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable i18n. Default locale `en`; add `fr`.
2. Collection type `article` (Localization on) with: localized text `title`; a **repeatable component** `sections` (component with localized text label), component field set to **localized**.
3. Create article in en: `title="EN title"`, `sections=[{label:"EN section"}]`. Publish.
4. Create the **fr** localization with different data: `title="FR title"`, `sections=[{label:"FR section"}]`. Publish.
5. GraphQL:
```
query {
  articles(locale: "fr", status: PUBLISHED) {
    title              # → "FR title"     ✅
    sections { label } # → "EN section"   ❌ (returns default-locale component)
  }
}
```
6. REST (same entry): `GET /api/articles?locale=fr&status=published&populate[sections]=true` → `sections[0].label = "FR section"` ✅

### Expected Behavior

**Expected**: GraphQL returns the **fr** component (`"FR section"`), consistent with the scalar field and with REST.
**Actual**: GraphQL returns the default-locale (`en`) component (`"EN section"`), while title is correctly `"FR title"`. `documentId(locale:"fr")` behaves the same.

Additional context: scalar-OK + component-wrong + REST-OK ⇒ the GraphQL populate step isn't propagating the operation locale to localized components/dynamic zones. Workaround: fetch that component via REST.

### Node Version

24.8.0

### Package Manager

npm

### Package Manager Version

11.6.0

### Strapi Version

5.50.0

### Operating System

MacOS

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

`@strapi/types` declares the admin forgot-password email template as a `string`, but both the default value and the runtime consumer treat it as an object of shape `{ subject, text, html }`.

Type (v5.50.0, `packages/core/types/src/core/config/admin.ts` L63-67):

```ts
export interface ForgotPassword {
  emailTemplate?: string;
  from?: string;
  replyTo?: string;
}
```

Reality:

- **Default value is an object** — `packages/core/admin/server/src/config/index.ts` sets `forgotPassword.emailTemplate = forgotPasswordTemplate`, and `config/email-templates/forgot-password.ts` default-exports `{ subject, text, html }`.
- **Runtime requires an object** — the admin auth service passes `strapi.config.get('admin.forgotPassword.emailTemplate')` as the `emailTemplate` argument of the email plugin's `sendTemplatedEmail` (`packages/core/admin/server/src/services/auth.ts` L79). `sendTemplatedEmail` validates that `Object.keys(emailTemplate)` contains `subject`, `text` and `html`, and throws otherwise (`packages/core/email/server/src/services/email.ts` L25-37).
- The email plugin already exports the matching shape: `EmailTemplate` in `packages/core/email/server/src/types.ts` (L36-41).

Impact: a TypeScript user who customizes `config/admin.ts` following the declared type (a `string`) gets a runtime error (`Following attributes are missing from your email template : subject, text, html`) when a forgot-password email is actually sent. Conversely, providing the correct object shape requires suppressing the type error — we currently work around it with an `as unknown as string` cast in our projects.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In a TypeScript Strapi 5.50.0 project, set a custom template in `config/admin.ts` following the declared type:

   ```ts
   forgotPassword: {
     emailTemplate: 'You can reset your password here: <%= url %>',
   },
   ```

2. `tsc` accepts it.
3. Trigger the admin forgot-password flow — `sendTemplatedEmail` throws `Following attributes are missing from your email template : subject, text, html`.
4. Providing the working shape `{ subject, text, html }` instead is rejected by the compiler (`Type '{ subject: string; ... }' is not assignable to type 'string'`).

### Expected Behavior

The declared type should match the runtime contract, e.g.:

```ts
export interface ForgotPassword {
  emailTemplate?: { subject: string; text: string; html?: string };
  from?: string;
  replyTo?: string;
}
```

or reference the email plugin's `EmailTemplate` interface.

PostgreSQL

### Javascript or Typescript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

Two messages in the email plugin translation catalog contain a bare `<email@host>` segment, which is invalid ICU MessageFormat when tag parsing is enabled (the default for `@formatjs/icu-messageformat-parser`, which react-intl uses under the hood).

`packages/core/email/admin/src/translations/en.json` (v5.50.0):

```json
"Settings.email.plugin.placeholder.defaultFrom": "ex: Strapi No-Reply <no-reply@strapi.io>",
"Settings.email.plugin.placeholder.defaultReplyTo": "ex: Strapi <example@strapi.io>"
```

The `<no-reply@strapi.io>` part is treated as an opening tag and the parser throws `INVALID_TAG`. Locale files that include these keys mirror the same raw form (e.g. `ja.json`), so a fix to `en.json` implies a coordinated fix of the mirrored locales.

This breaks any tooling that runs the catalogs through the ICU parser (message validation, extraction, TMS pipelines) and forces localization tooling to special-case these two messages. Discovered while preparing #26687.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In a Strapi 5.50.0 project (the parser is already in the dependency tree via `@strapi/admin` → react-intl), run:

   ```bash
   node -e "require('@formatjs/icu-messageformat-parser').parse('ex: Strapi No-Reply <no-reply@strapi.io>')"
   ```

2. The parser throws `INVALID_TAG` (verified with `@formatjs/icu-messageformat-parser` 2.7.6). The `defaultReplyTo` value fails the same way.

### Expected Behavior

Catalog messages should be valid ICU MessageFormat. Escaping the angle brackets with ICU single quotes keeps the rendered text identical and parses cleanly (verified against the same parser version):

```json
"Settings.email.plugin.placeholder.defaultFrom": "ex: Strapi No-Reply '<no-reply@strapi.io>'",
"Settings.email.plugin.placeholder.defaultReplyTo": "ex: Strapi '<example@strapi.io>'"
```

Alternatively, drop the angle-bracket form from the example text entirely (e.g. `ex: no-reply@strapi.io`).

### Logs

```shell
Error: INVALID_TAG
    at createError (.../@formatjs/icu-messageformat-parser/error.js)
```

### Bug Description

## Setup / Environment (for quick triage)

- **Strapi version:** `5.48.1` (also reproduced on `5.47.1` and probably all versions in v5 have this issue)
- **Affected packages:**
  - `@strapi/admin`
  - `@strapi/content-manager`
- **Project type:** npm monorepo with workspaces; CMS workspace depends on `@strapi/strapi`
- **Node / npm:** Node `22.14.0`, npm `10.9.2`
- **Operating System:** Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Linux 6.17.0-22-generic)
- **Registry:** Private Artifactory npm virtual repo (**JFrog Curation enabled**)
- **Supply-chain tool:** JFrog CLI `jf curation-audit` (`jf ca --working-dirs='containers/cms'`) v2.111.0 with `--run-native`
- **Workspace configuration in project's root package.json:**
```
"workspaces": [
  "containers/frontend",
  "containers/backend",
  "containers/cms",
  "containers/jobs"
]
```

## Describe the problem

Strapi v5 declares CodeMirror v5 using an **npm package alias**:

```json
"codemirror5": "npm:codemirror@^5.65.11"
```

This is intentional so Strapi can use CodeMirror 5 (admin JSON editor) alongside CodeMirror 6 (@uiw/react-codemirror via @strapi/design-system) in the same dependency tree.

However, this alias naming causes enterprise OSS supply-chain scanners, here JFrog Curation via **jf ca** to fail with a 404 when auditing any project that depends on Strapi — even though npm ci / npm install succeed and the lockfile is correct.

```
Dependency chain
my-cms-app
└── @strapi/strapi@5.48.1
    ├── @strapi/admin
    │   └── codemirror5 → npm:codemirror@5.65.21
    └── @strapi/content-manager
        └── codemirror5 → npm:codemirror@5.65.21 (deduped)
```
**Source:**

https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/v5.48.1/packages/core/admin/package.json
https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/packages/core/admin/package.json

**jf ca** fails with:

```
[🚨Error] failed sending HEAD request to
https://<artifactory>/artifactory/api/npm/<repo>/codemirror5/-/codemirror5-5.65.21.tgz
for package 'codemirror5:5.65.21'. Status-code: 404
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a Strapi v5 app (or monorepo workspace) with @strapi/strapi@5.48.1.
2. Run npm install against a JFrog-curated Artifactory npm registry.
3. Confirm install succeeds: `npm ls codemirror5`
4. Expected tree: `└── codemirror5@npm:codemirror@5.65.21`
5. Run JFrog curation audit from the CMS project directory:
`jf ca --working-dirs=containers/cms --run-native`

**Actual behavior**
**jf ca** fails with:

```
[🚨Error] failed sending HEAD request to
https://<artifactory>/artifactory/api/npm/<repo>/codemirror5/-/codemirror5-5.65.21.tgz
for package 'codemirror5:5.65.21'. Status-code: 404
```

The scanner requests a tarball named **codemirror5**, which does not exist on **npm or Artifactory**. The real published package is **codemirror@5.65.21**.

### Expected Behavior

Supply-chain / curation tooling, here **Jfrog** should be able to audit Strapi-based projects without hard failure.

At minimum, we would appreciate one of:

- Strapi documents that the codemirror5 npm alias is incompatible with some enterprise curation scanners today, **with recommended workarounds**.
- Strapi considers an alternative dependency strategy that avoids npm aliases but still allows CM5 + CM6 coexistence.
- Coordination with JFrog if Strapi believes alias-aware resolution should remain a tooling responsibility.

### Logs

```shell

```

_No response_

### Media

_No response_

### Additional information

## Impact

- CMS CI pipelines fail at supply-chain audit stage (before Docker build/deploy).
- Teams cannot obtain curation waivers for codemirror5 because no such package exists on the registry — the failure is a 404, not a policy block.
- Affects any organization using JFrog Curation (and potentially other scanners with similar alias handling).

## Workarounds attempted (none sufficient)

- npm overrides to pin codemirror@5.65.21
**Result**: Lockfile already correct; jf ca still HEADs codemirror5-…tgz

**Result**: Not possible — package name does not exist on registry

# Homepage should ignore stale permissions in draft/publish-only queries

## Node Version

v24.12.0

## Package Manager

Yarn

## Package Manager Version

4.12.0

## Strapi Version

5.49.0 (`fix/lint-warnings` branch, PR #26818 context)

## Operating System

macOS 26.5 (Darwin)

## Database

SQLite (default `examples/getstarted` sandbox; bug is database-agnostic)

## Javascript or Typescript

TypeScript

## Reproduction URL

N/A - identified from code review and local source inspection.

## Bug Description

The Content Manager homepage service should explicitly ignore stale permission subjects when building draft/publish-only recent document queries.

`getContentTypesMeta` now skips missing content types, but `queryLastDocuments(..., true)` still calls `contentTypes.hasDraftAndPublish(strapi.contentType(uid))` for every permitted subject before that guard runs.

Current behavior is tolerant only because `strapi.contentType(uid)` returns `undefined` for a missing UID and `contentTypes.hasDraftAndPublish(undefined)` currently returns `false`. The homepage publish flow is therefore relying on helper tolerance rather than enforcing the invariant that stale permission subjects are dropped before content-type predicates run. There is also no focused test for stale UIDs in the `draftAndPublishOnly=true` path.

Affected package: `@strapi/content-manager` server homepage service.

Relevant code:

- Review comment: https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/26818#discussion_r3489996549
- Homepage service: https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/packages/core/content-manager/server/src/homepage/services/homepage.ts
- Current content type lookup: https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/packages/core/core/src/Strapi.ts
- Current `hasDraftAndPublish` helper: https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/packages/core/utils/src/content-types.ts

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an admin role with a stale `plugin::content-manager.explorer.read` permission subject whose UID no longer exists in `strapi.contentTypes`.
2. Request the homepage recently published endpoint: `GET /content-manager/homepage/recent-documents?action=publish`.
3. The service enters `getRecentlyPublishedDocuments()`, then `queryLastDocuments(..., true)`.
4. The stale UID is evaluated by `contentTypes.hasDraftAndPublish(strapi.contentType(uid))` before the later `getContentTypesMeta` missing-content-type guard can skip it.

## Expected Behavior

The homepage service should explicitly filter stale permission subjects before evaluating draft/publish metadata.

Missing content type UIDs should be ignored in both homepage recent document paths:

- `action=update` / `draftAndPublishOnly=false`
- `action=publish` / `draftAndPublishOnly=true`

## Logs

N/A. Current code does not prove a live crash in this checkout because `hasDraftAndPublish(undefined)` returns `false`.

## Code Snippets

Current risky path:

```ts
const allowedContentTypeUids = draftAndPublishOnly
  ? permittedContentTypes.filter((uid) => {
      return contentTypes.hasDraftAndPublish(strapi.contentType(uid));
    })
  : permittedContentTypes;
```

Recommended fix:

```ts
const allowedContentTypeUids = draftAndPublishOnly
  ? permittedContentTypes.filter((uid) => {
      const contentType = strapi.contentTypes[uid];
      return contentType !== undefined && contentTypes.hasDraftAndPublish(contentType);
    })
  : permittedContentTypes;
```

Add a focused homepage service test asserting a stale permission subject is ignored when `draftAndPublishOnly === true` and that the draft/publish predicate is not called with `undefined`.

Optionally, in `getCountDocuments`, use `meta.contentType.collectionName` instead of `strapi.contentType(meta.uid).collectionName` because `meta` is already built only from existing content types.

## Media

N/A

## Additional information

Existing `homepage.test.ts` covers stale UIDs for `queryLastDocuments({ sort: 'updatedAt:desc' })`, but not the publish-only path used by `getRecentlyPublishedDocuments()`.

The original review comment says `strapi.contentType(uid)` throws for stale UIDs. Local source inspection shows it returns the registry lookup result, so the safer issue framing is: stale permission subjects are not explicitly filtered in the draft/publish-only flow, and the code lacks a regression test for that invariant.

## Confirmation Checklist

- [ ] I have checked the existing [issues](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues) for duplicates. [NEEDS INPUT]
- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
items.title: Homepage should ignore stale permissions in draft/publish-only queries

yarn

### Operating System

Other

### Database

Other

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

**Strapi version:** 5.x (latest)
**Node.js version:** 20.x
**Database:** any
**OS:** any

**Describe the bug:**
When a content editor is mid-save (HTTP POST/PUT request in-flight) and a
schema change triggers a server reload, `reloader.ts` calls
`process.send('reload')` immediately. The parent process kills the worker
with no drain period. The in-flight save request is terminated with a
connection reset — the editor loses their work with no warning.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Open the Content Manager and start editing a long article.
2. In a second browser tab (as admin), open Content-Type Builder and
   save a field change, triggering a server reload.
3. Switch back to the first tab and click Save.
4. The save fails with a network error / connection reset.

**Expected behaviour:**
The server should stop accepting new connections but allow in-flight
requests up to a configurable timeout (e.g. 30s) to complete before
sending the reload signal. This is standard graceful shutdown behaviour
(Node.js `httpServer.closeIdleConnections()` + drain window).

**Relevant code:**
packages/core/core/src/services/reloader.ts — the `reload()` function
calls `process.send('reload')` with no drain:
```ts
if (strapi.config.get('autoReload')) {
  process.send?.('reload'); // ← no drain, kills in-flight requests
}
```
packages/core/core/src/services/server/http-server.ts — the HTTP server
has no SIGTERM/graceful-shutdown handler.

**Additional context:**
Issue #5912 requested graceful shutdown in v3/v4 but was closed as
"handled in v4". It did not address the v5 reloader's reload path or
production HTTP drain. This is a distinct regression in v5 behaviour.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a Strapi v5 project with autoReload enabled (development mode):
   `yarn strapi develop`

2. Open the Content Manager in the browser and navigate to any Collection Type
   with a large content entry (e.g. an article with a Rich Text field).

3. Begin editing the entry — type a significant amount of content so the
   save request will take a moment to complete.

4. In a second browser tab (same admin user or another admin), open the
   Content-Type Builder and add or remove any field from any content type,
   then click Save. This triggers reloader.ts to call process.send('reload').

5. Immediately switch back to the first tab and click the Save button
   before the server has fully restarted.

6. Observe that the save request fails with a network error or connection
   reset (browser DevTools → Network tab shows the POST/PUT request as
   "failed" or "cancelled" with no response).

7. The content editor receives no meaningful error message — the work
   written in step 3 is lost silently.

Expected: The server should finish handling the in-flight save request
before reloading. The editor's save should succeed or, at minimum, the
editor should receive a clear retry prompt.

Actual: The request is terminated mid-flight. No data is saved.
No warning is shown to the editor.

### Expected Behavior

When a schema change triggers a server reload, any HTTP requests that are
already in-flight (e.g. a content editor's save request) should be allowed
to complete before the reload signal is sent to the parent process.

Specifically:
1. The server should stop accepting new incoming connections immediately.
2. Existing in-flight requests should be given a configurable grace period
   (e.g. 30 seconds, via a server.shutdownTimeout config option) to finish.
3. Once all in-flight requests have completed — or the timeout is reached —
   only then should process.send('reload') be called.
4. If the timeout is reached before all requests finish, the server should
   log a warning and proceed with the reload, rather than hanging indefinitely.

The content editor's save should succeed normally. If the timeout is
genuinely exceeded (an unusually slow request), the editor should receive
a proper HTTP error response they can retry — not a silent connection reset
that loses their work with no feedback.

This is standard Node.js graceful shutdown behaviour, achievable with
httpServer.closeIdleConnections() combined with httpServer.close() and
a drain timeout, both of which are available in Node.js 20+.

### Logs

```shell

```

### Node Version

### Package Manager Version

10.9.7

### Strapi Version

5.47.1

### Operating System

Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

In the Content Manager list view, filtering a `datetime` field (including the built-in **Created At** and **Updated At** filters) with the **is** (`$eq`) operator almost never returns results, even when entries clearly exist for the selected date/time.

Root cause is a precision mismatch between the filter input and the stored values:

- The filter UI offers `is` / `is not` for `datetime` attributes (`getFilterList` in `packages/core/admin/admin/src/components/Filters.tsx`, the `datetime` case returns `BASE_FILTERS + NUMERIC_FILTERS`).
- The value input is the generic `DateTimePicker`, which emits `date.toISOString()` with seconds and milliseconds zeroed (`packages/core/admin/admin/src/components/FormInputs/DateTime.tsx`). The design-system `TimePicker` only offers `HH:mm` options (15 minute step by default), so the UI cannot express seconds at all.
- Stored `created_at` / `updated_at` values have sub-second precision (e.g. `2026-06-09 20:25:38.123`).
- There is no server-side special casing of `$eq` on datetime attributes (checked content-manager server and `core/utils` query conversion), so the query is a literal `WHERE created_at = '2026-06-09T20:25:00.000Z'`, which only matches rows that happen to land exactly on a zero-second boundary.

Range operators (`is greater than`, `is less than`, etc.) work as expected since they don't require an exact match. This is consistent with what users report: "is" returns nothing, "greater than" works.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create any collection type and add a few entries.
2. Open the list view in the Content Manager.
3. Add a filter: **Created At** + **is** + select today's date (any time).
4. Observe that no results are returned even though entries created today exist.
5. Change the operator to **is greater than or equal to** with the same value: results are returned.

### Expected Behavior

Filtering a datetime field with **is** should match the user's intent at the precision the picker can express, i.e. match the selected minute (or the whole day when only a date is meaningful), instead of performing an exact sub-second timestamp comparison that the UI cannot express.

Two possible directions:

1. Transform `$eq` / `$ne` on datetime fields into a range covering the selected minute (e.g. `$gte` selected minute / `$lt` next minute). Note the filter chip rendering in `Filters.tsx` (`List` / `getFilterDetails`) currently skips object-shaped values, so chip display needs to be handled as part of this.
2. Alternatively, stop offering `is` / `is not` for `datetime` attributes and keep the null checks and range operators, so the UI doesn't expose an operator it can't express.

### Logs

```shell
No errors are logged. The query executes successfully and returns 0 results.
```

### Code Snippets

_No response_

### Media

_No response_

### Additional information

- Reported by an enterprise customer via support (Internal TID 9286). Confirmed via the customer's screen recording and against the codebase on `develop`.
- Not a regression: the behavior has existed since the operator list and `DateTimePicker` input were introduced. Reproduces on any OS/database/package manager.
- Timezone adds a second layer of confusion on top of this: the picker converts local time to a UTC ISO string, so even a minute-range match needs to be done on the UTC instant the picker produced.
- Workaround given to the customer: combine two filters, **is greater than or equal to** day start and **is less than** the next day (filters combine as `$and`).

### Confirmation Checklist

- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

There is no visible scroll indicator, so users — and even developers spending hours debugging — believe the locale is missing from the data entirely. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure 5 or more locales in Settings → Internationalization (e.g. en, fr, de, nl-NL, es) 2. Open the content manager on any localized collection type 3. Click the locale picker dropdown (list view filter or edit view header) 4. Observe: only 4 locales are visible; the 5th and beyond appear absent ### Expected Behavior All configured locales should be visible, or there should be a clear visual indicator (scroll arrow, scrollbar, item count) that more locales exist below the visible area. ### Logs ```shell ``` ### Code Snippets _No response_ ### Media The scrollbar is so discret that the user can miss it. ### Additional information Actual behavior The SingleSelect component from @strapi/design-system applies max-height: 15.6rem to the dropdown content, which fits approximately 4 items. ## Summary

`@strapi-community/plugin-seo` is still marketplace-listed and recommended as the SEO plugin for Strapi 5, but its source repository was archived in December 2025 with no public successor, leaving Strapi 5 ergonomic improvements unfilled.

## Details

- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@strapi-community/plugin-seo (2.1.1, published 2025)
- Source: https://github.com/strapi-community/plugin-seo — archived 2025-12-02
- Original upstream: https://github.com/notum-cz/strapi-plugin-seo — also archived
- Issues are disabled on both repos. No fork has been published under the `strapi-community` org. No "moved to…" pointer is referenced from the marketplace listing.

Concrete consequence: the plugin still bootstraps via the legacy `app.getPlugin('content-manager').injectComponent('editView', 'right-links', { … })` injection zone. In Strapi 5 this slot renders **below** all proper side panels (Information, Releases, plugin panels registered via `addEditViewSidePanel`), so the SEO summary is visually disconnected from the panel stack despite being conceptually a side panel.

Migrating to the newer `apis.addEditViewSidePanel((panels) => […])` API is a ~10-line change and would normally land as a small PR, but the archived state blocks the usual contribution path.

## Ask

1. **Marketplace policy** — what is the intended user signal when a community plugin's source is archived? A "no longer maintained" badge on the marketplace listing, or a delist threshold, would help downstream users decide whether to fork.
2. **Org plans for `strapi-community/plugin-seo`** — is the team planning to unarchive, transfer ownership, or replace this plugin? If so, where should follow-up activity go?
3. **Successor recommendation** — if neither of the above, is there a maintained Strapi 5 SEO plugin the team can point users to?

## Environment

- `@strapi-community/plugin-seo`: 2.1.1
- `@strapi/strapi`: 5.x
- Browser, OS: not relevant — repo metadata only.

## Reproduction

Not a bug report — purely an ecosystem / governance question about an archived marketplace-listed plugin.

### Node Version

22.22.3

### Package Manager

npm

### Package Manager Version

10.x (bundled with node:22-alpine)

### Strapi Version

5.46.0

### Operating System

Docker/Podman/LXC

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Bug Description

In a TypeScript Strapi v5 project, `strapi start` calls `tsUtils.isUsingTypeScript(appDir)` to decide whether to load configs from `dist/config/` (TS project, compiled output) or `./config/` (plain JS project). The function does two things:

1. Checks for the existence of `tsconfig.json`.
2. Runs `tsc` against the configured `rootDir` to verify the project compiles.

The second step **requires the TypeScript source files** (`src/` and `config/`) to be present in the runtime working directory, even though `strapi start` only consumes the compiled `dist/` output afterwards. If sources are missing, `tsc` aborts with `TS18003: No inputs were found in config file 'tsconfig.json'` and Strapi falls back to treating the project as a JS project — at which point it looks for configs at `./config/`, doesn't find them either, and crashes with `TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'client' of 'db.config.connection' as it is undefined` (because the database config never loaded, so `db.config` is empty).

For containerised production deployments this means the final image **must** ship the entire TypeScript source tree in addition to the compiled `dist/`, even though the sources are never executed at runtime. That's typically 50+ MB of dead weight and exposes pre-compiled source paths in the image.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `npx create-strapi-app@latest ts-bug --typescript`
2. `cd ts-bug && npm install && npm run build` → produces `dist/`
3. Create a minimal production runtime image (multi-stage):

```dockerfile
FROM node:22-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm install
COPY . .
ENV NODE_ENV=production
RUN npm run build

FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm install --omit=dev
COPY --from=builder /app/dist     ./dist
COPY --from=builder /app/.strapi  ./.strapi
COPY public ./public
# Note: NOT copying tsconfig.json, src/, or config/
CMD ["node_modules/.bin/strapi", "start"]
```

4. Build + run.

Observed:

```
TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'client' of 'db.config.connection' as it is undefined.
    at Object.getDialect (/app/node_modules/@strapi/database/dist/dialects/index.js:36:13)
    at new Database (/app/node_modules/@strapi/database/dist/index.js:145:32)
    at /app/node_modules/@strapi/core/dist/Strapi.js:214:20
```

The error is misleading — the real cause is that `isUsingTypeScript()` returned `false`, so `loadConfiguration()` looked at `./config/` (which doesn't exist) instead of `./dist/config/` (which does exist and was correctly compiled).

### Expected Behavior

In production mode (`NODE_ENV=production`), `isUsingTypeScript()` should detect a TypeScript project from the existence of `dist/config/` (or another deterministic compiled-output marker) without invoking `tsc` against the source tree. The check should pass even when only the compiled output is present.

This would let production images ship only `dist/`, `.strapi/`, and `public/` — the actual artefacts the runtime executes — with no source files.

### Logs

See "Steps to Reproduce".

### Additional information

**Current workaround**: copy `tsconfig.json`, `src/`, and `config/` into the runtime image alongside `dist/`. This works because `tsc` then has inputs to type-check, but adds ~50 MB of source files that are never read at runtime.

Reference implementation that hits this and ships sources as the workaround:
- https://github.com/XMV-Solutions-GmbH/website/blob/main/cms/Dockerfile

### Confirmation Checklist

- I have checked the existing issues for duplicates.
- I agree to follow the project's Code of Conduct.

### Bug Description

We got the new responseType option for the `getFetchClient`, which is great in itself. See https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/25974

However, if we use this now and the server send back an error, for example a 400 bad request one, this will not be passed through.

Example:
```js
try {
  const csvData = await get('/lms/reports/download', {
    responseType: 'text',
  });
} catch (error) {
  // no error given here other than "FetchError: Server Error"
  console.log(error)
}
```
If we now get a  bad request error back
```json
{
    "data": null,
    "error": {
        "status": 400,
        "name": "BadRequestError",
        "message": "Type is required",
        "details": {}
    }
}
```

```
FetchError: Server Error

    at executeRequest (getFetchClient.ts:411:16)
    at async withTokenRefresh (getFetchClient.ts:342:14)
```

This make sit hard to use, because obviously errors can be common and we need to give feedback to the suer on what is wrong.

items.body:
### Node Version

20.20.2

### Package Manager

npm

### Package Manager Version

10.2.0

### Strapi Version

5.42.0

### Operating System

MacOS

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

## Summary
When running Strapi under Node 20+ in ESM mode, Strapi fails to start because compiled ESM files import `lodash/fp` as named exports and/or as a directory specifier. Errors observed include:

- ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: .../node_modules/@strapi/core/node_modules/lodash/fp/index.jsx
- SyntaxError: The requested module 'lodash/fp.js' does not provide an export named 'get'

## Reproduction steps
1. Clone a minimal reproduction repository (or use the steps below).
2. Node version: 20.x
3. npm install
4. npm run develop
5. Observe the startup error and stack trace.

Minimal repro steps
- package.json includes Strapi v5.42.0 and Node 20.
- Run `npm install` then `npm run develop`.

## Logs
Example errors from a real repro:
- `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../node_modules/@strapi/core/node_modules/lodash/fp/index.jsx'`
- `SyntaxError: The requested module 'lodash/fp.js' does not provide an export named 'get'`

## Root cause
- Lodash v4 `fp` is a CommonJS module that exposes a default export (an object). It does not provide named ESM exports.
- Strapi’s compiled ESM files use named imports like `import { get } from 'lodash/fp'` and directory specifiers like `import 'lodash/fp'`. Under Node ESM:
  - Directory imports require `exports` in the package to resolve safely.
  - Named imports from a CommonJS default export are invalid and throw `does not provide an export named` errors.

## Impact
- Strapi fails to start in Node 20+ ESM environments for many users.
- Workarounds (shims, patching node_modules, nested proxies) are fragile and not ideal for teams or CI.

## Suggested solutions
1. **Preferred**: Publish an ESM-compatible build or add `exports` entries so `lodash/fp` resolves to an ESM-compatible module. This could be:
   - Add an ESM build for Strapi packages that uses ESM-compatible dependencies or
   - Add compatibility wrappers for CJS-only dependencies.
2. **Alternative**: Update Strapi build output to:
   - Emit explicit `.js` specifiers for imports, and
   - Use default imports for `lodash/fp` and destructure (or otherwise consume the default) so code does not rely on named ESM imports from a CJS module.
3. **Docs**: Add a short note in the migration/installation docs about Node 20 ESM pitfalls and recommended Node/npm layouts.

## Minimal patch offer
I can provide a minimal patch that:
- Replaces `import { x } from 'lodash/fp'` with `import fp from 'lodash/fp.js'; const { x } = fp;`
- Replaces `require('lodash/fp')` with `require('lodash/fp.js')`
- Adds tests that boot Strapi in ESM mode under Node 20

If maintainers prefer a different approach (exports map, switching to lodash-es, or build changes), I can adapt the PR.

## Environment
- Strapi version: 5.42.0
- Node: 20.20.2
- npm: (user’s npm version)

5.39.0

### Operating System

Other Linux

### Database

SQLite

### Javascript or Typescript

Javascript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

When using `@strapi/provider-upload-aws-s3` with a private bucket and signed URLs enabled, images embedded in text/richtext fields (e.g. via the WYSIWYG editor) store the signed URL directly in the database as a static string. Unlike media-type fields — which receive fresh signed URLs on every retrieval via `signFileUrlsOnDocumentService()` — these embedded URLs expire (default 15 minutes) and are never refreshed.

The root cause is that the `signEntityMedia` visitor in `packages/core/upload/server/src/services/extensions/utils.ts` only processes attributes where `attribute.type === 'media'`. It does not parse or re-sign URLs embedded in richtext/text field content.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure `@strapi/provider-upload-aws-s3` with a private bucket (ACL set to `private`) and signed URLs enabled
2. Create a content type with a richtext or text (markdown) field
3. Upload an image via the media library and embed it into the richtext field using the WYSIWYG editor
4. Save the content entry
5. Wait for the signed URL to expire (default: 15 minutes)
6. Fetch the content via the API or reload the admin panel — the embedded image URL is now broken/returns 403

### Expected Behavior

Signed URLs embedded in text/richtext fields should be refreshed on content retrieval, the same way URLs in media-type fields are refreshed. The document service signing logic should also handle asset URLs found within text/richtext content.

### Logs

_No response_

### Code Snippets

Example S3 provider config with private bucket:

```js
// config/plugins.js
module.exports = ({ env }) => ({
  upload: {
    config: {
      provider: 'aws-s3',
      providerOptions: {
        s3Options: {
          credentials: {
            accessKeyId: env('AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID'),
            secretAccessKey: env('AWS_ACCESS_SECRET'),
          },
          region: env('AWS_REGION'),
          params: {
            ACL: 'private',
            signedUrlExpires: 15 * 60, // 15 minutes (default)
            Bucket: env('AWS_BUCKET'),
          },
        },
      },
    },
  },
});
```

_No response_

Related to Pylon support ticket 7616.

Affected packages: `@strapi/provider-upload-aws-s3`, `@strapi/upload`, `@strapi/content-manager`

This error has been [reported by multiple users across 30+ closed issues](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20removeChild&page=1) (closed by bot, not resolved). None of the closed threads contain a confirmed fix or root cause. I cannot reproduce this reliably myself, but I have consistent reports from clients running Strapi in production.

**The core problem being reported here is not just the error itself — it's that Strapi provides zero debugging context when this happens. There is no component name, no field, no route, no action that caused it. Users and developers have no actionable information to debug or report meaningfully.** And that's probably why none of these problems have ever been solved.

Unable to provide a reliable reproduction. Neither OS nor Node version makes change.

Either:

_If you've encountered this error and found a fix or a workaround — even a partial one — please share it in the comments. ### Node Version

bun:1.3.6-alpine

### NPM/Yarn/PNPM Version

bun 1.3.6

### Strapi Version

v4.26.1 (also applies to v5?)

### Operating System

Other

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Javascript or Typescript

Typescript

### Reproduction URL

_No response_

### Bug Description

We are seeing duplicate users despite having the `unique_email` setting for the users-permissions plugin set to `true`. Considering the timestamp difference in `created_at` is often in the order of (10s) ms we suspect a race condition:

```sql
WITH duplicates AS (
    -- 1. Identify emails that appear more than once (case-insensitive)
    SELECT LOWER(email) as norm_email
    FROM up_users
    GROUP BY LOWER(email)
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
)
SELECT 
    u.id,
    -- 2. Masking Logic: First 3 chars + '***' + everything from @ onwards
    LEFT(u.email, 3) || '***' || SUBSTRING(u.email FROM POSITION('@' IN u.email)) as masked_email,
    u.created_at,
    -- 3. Calculate difference from the previous duplicate row
    u.created_at - LAG(u.created_at) OVER (
        PARTITION BY LOWER(u.email) 
        ORDER BY u.created_at
    ) as time_since_prev
FROM up_users u
JOIN duplicates d ON LOWER(u.email) = d.norm_email
ORDER BY LOWER(u.email), u.created_at;
   id   |          masked_email           |       created_at        |    time_since_prev     
--------+---------------------------------+-------------------------+------------------------
  97757 | 23a***@gmail.com                | 2025-07-17 08:02:16.471 | 
  97758 | 23a***@gmail.com                | 2025-07-17 08:02:16.477 | 00:00:00.006
 101149 | aam***@gmail.com                | 2025-09-19 15:14:57.422 | 
 101150 | aam***@gmail.com                | 2025-09-19 15:14:57.438 | 00:00:00.016
 107306 | abd***@gmail.com                | 2026-01-05 15:36:10.324 | 
 107307 | abd***@gmail.com                | 2026-01-05 15:36:10.324 | 00:00:00
 106987 | abd***@gmail.com                | 2026-01-01 11:59:35.101 | 
 106988 | abd***@gmail.com                | 2026-01-01 11:59:35.124 | 00:00:00.023
 106564 | abd***@gmail.com                | 2025-12-26 07:25:53.476 | 
 106565 | abd***@gmail.com                | 2025-12-26 07:25:53.495 | 00:00:00.019
 101607 | abo***@gmail.com                | 2025-10-01 11:04:27.323 | 
 101608 | abo***@gmail.com                | 2025-10-01 11:04:27.327 | 00:00:00.004
```

After some digging I discovered that the uniqueness constraint for the email actually doesn't exist for the `up_users` field on the table as it would for other fields that you can add on the `up_users` collection. Perhaps this was initially done because of the toggle for the uniqueness constraint in the admin panel. It would be great if we can also enforce this at the database level so that next queries in our case get rejected.

### Steps to Reproduce

Make multiple parallel calls to the auth callback `/api/auth/google/callback?access_token=...`

### Expected Behavior

The second calls should return the user and not create another one.

### Logs
